item.title: The covering radius of RM(1,9) is precisely 242
item.description: arXiv:2611.00070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Mullet code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, and the determination of $\rho(1,9)$ is a long-standing open question. We give a computer-assisted proof that $\rho(1,9)=242$, leveraging the classification of the $349$ orbits in $\text{RM}(3,9)/\text{RM}(2,9)$ under $\text{GL}(9,2)$ [1,3]. The notebook to verify the computer search portion, Verify_RM(1,9).ipynb, contains all data and recomputes each check, and may be found in the repository https://github.com/FreemanSlaughter/Covering-Radius.
item.dc:creator: Xiang-Dong Hou, Evelyn Sabo, Freeman Slaughter

item.title: Applying Changes to LDPC Codes by Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2611.00082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The 2-switch operation for reducing the number of short cycles in Tanner graphs of LDPC codes has been utilized in some works. If this operation is appropriately applied to a 2-induced matching in a bipartite graph, then it surely preserves the bipartiteness of the graph. With a 2-induced matching, we have only one choice for applying this type of change to the graph. Using 3-induced matchings creates more potential and flexibility to apply certain changes to the Tanner graph. We present a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a 3-induced matching in bipartite graphs with girth at least 6. A 3-induced matching helps us to have more choices for applying a change to a bipartite graph while surely preserving the bipartiteness of the graph and keeping the degree sequences unchanged. Among all changes that we consider, we select the best change for reducing the number of cycles of length 6. The eigenvalues of subgraphs are used to reach a 3-induced matching, and a condition in some steps can be checked to ensure that the subgraph has at least one 3-induced matching. We present some numerical results regarding the steps at which the condition that guarantees the existence of a 3-induced matching is checked.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Eshraghi Dehaghani, Sara Saeedi Madani, Dariush Kiani

item.title: HideOut - User Protection Against Localization with Throughput Guarantees in Mobile Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.00088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Channel state information (CSI) in cellular networks is primarily used to maintain quality of service (QoS), yet it leaks privacy-sensitive information, in particular the user equipment's (UE) location. CSI is reported in plaintext on a publicly available schedule; thus, capturing it on the air and using a well trained AI model to localize the UE is straightforward. This simplicity in the attack execution makes it a serious privacy vulnerability. Using conventional privacy enhancing techniques, such as additive perturbation from differential privacy, to protect location data can potentially degrade the downlink communication quality. We present HideOut, a client-side defense mechanism that preserves the user's location from neural-based localization methods, while maintaining their downlink Spectral Efficiency (SE). Unlike generic adversarial attacks, HideOut treats downlink SE as a strict constraint in an optimization setting. Under maximum ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming, we show that a user-selected SE loss budget can be converted into an angular rate-feasible constraint on the reported channel vector. HideOut then performs gradient-based localization obfuscation while projecting each update onto this rate-feasible set. We evaluate HideOut against four CSI-based localization architectures under both white-box and black-box assumptions. Across models, HideOut increases localization ambiguity (error) from approximately $1--2$ m to $72--85$ m while keeping downlink SE loss within a $1\%$ budget. These results show that CSI-based localization can be substantially degraded at negligible communication quality loss when adversarial perturbations are made aware of the wireless link.
item.dc:creator: Navidreza Asadi, Michele Guardiani, Wolfgang Kellerer, Jafar Aco Mohammadi

item.title: Energy-Efficient UAV Covert Communications via Metaheuristic Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.00090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wireless communication systems increasingly require not only confidentiality but also transmission undetectability, motivating covert communications. This paper studies an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) enabled covert communication system where a UAV serves a legitimate receiver in the presence of multiple active and colluding wardens with imperfect location information. We maximize covert energy efficiency (CEE) by jointly optimizing the UAV's 3D trajectory and transmit power while accounting for energy. To address the resulting non-convex problem with robust covertness constraints, we develop Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)-based metaheuristic algorithms and compare them with a Block Coordinate Descent with Successive Convex Approximation (BCD-SCA) benchmark. Numerical results show that the proposed methods improve CEE while satisfying covertness constraints.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Minh Quan, Tran Thanh Thu, Nguyen The Ngoc Khue, Ninh Thi Thanh Tam, Trinh Van Chien

item.title: Comments on "Multidimensional Costas Arrays and Their Periodicity"
item.description: arXiv:2611.00098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rubio and Torres conjectured that a multidimensional Costas array, defined by a bijection between two boxes of integer points whose domain has at least as many dimensions as its image, can stay Costas in every window of its periodic extension only if its order is a power of two fixed by the dimension of the domain. We give a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order $6$, with a two-dimensional domain and a two-dimensional image, so the conjecture is false. The verification reduces to $36$ windows. It has been confirmed by computer and in the Lean proof assistant. The array also meets with equality the pigeonhole bound that Rubio and Torres use for their non-existence results, so that bound is tight.
item.dc:creator: Shiv Munagala

item.title: A Counterexample to the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.00156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a counterexample to the non-abelian Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture. The construction comes from an equivalent maximal-coupling entropy inequality, for which a counterexample can be found in a lower-dimensional group. We give an explicit cardinality counterexample in $D_4^{14}$, the fourteenth direct power of the dihedral group of order $8$.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Nair, Aref Namayandeh, Zhaobang Zhu

item.title: Beyond Typical Strings: Sampling the Complexity Landscape
item.description: arXiv:2611.00162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uniform random sampling of strings is overwhelmingly dominated by high-complexity strings, leaving the much smaller set of low- and intermediate-complexity strings largely unexplored. Here, we adapt the nested neutral set estimator (NNSE), a Monte Carlo rare-event sampling method, to estimate the distribution P(K) of complexity values for binary strings of fixed length. NNSE allows us to explore the full complexity landscape, including exponentially rare low-complexity regions that are inaccessible to direct sampling, for string lengths up to several hundred. We apply the method to several widely used complexity measures: Lempel-Ziv 76 (LZ76), Lempel-Ziv 78 (LZ78), context tree weighting (CTW), the block decomposition method (BDM), and block entropy. We further introduce uniform complexity weighting (UCW), which gives equal weight to different complexity levels rather than to individual strings. This approach provides a dataset-independent framework for comparing complexity measures across their full range and reveals substantial differences between measures for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are largely hidden by conventional uniform sampling. Using the NNSE to perform UCW sampling allows us to compare complexity measures across their full range in a dataset-independent way. This reveals differences in their behavior for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are practically inaccessible to conventional uniform sampling.
item.dc:creator: Abdurrahman Hadi Erturk, Joshua Sharkey, Nora S Martin, Kamal Dingle, Ard A Louis

item.title: A new upper bound for $A(19,6,8)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute Polak's bound $A_4(19,6,8)$ for binary constant weight codes, obtaining the numerical value $673.04001$. An exact rational certificate gives $A_4(19,6,8)\le 673.0400143064802474039375132665301315202504$, and hence $A(19,6,8)\le 673$. This improves the upper bound $693$ listed in Brouwer's table. The certificate is verified by a separate program using exact rational arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Chang

item.title: Equal Hamming Weights at Fixed Root Order and Applications to Constacyclic MDS Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.00637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a fixed positive integer $n>1$, we study the prime powers $q$ coprime to $n$ for which all monic irreducible factors of $\Phi_n$ over $\F_q$ have the same coefficient Hamming weight. Cyclotomic orbit coefficients give a finite, effective classification of these fields. Outside finitely many computable characteristics, every factor has the support of its characteristic-zero orbit polynomial; the uniform condition $p>2^{\varphi(n)}$ suffices. In each remaining characteristic, extension exponents reduce to divisors of $\ord_n(p)$, and an integer variance identity expressed by polynomial gcd degrees decides equal weight. The same coefficient data determine the full weight distribution. As an application, we prove that an MDS constacyclic code with an irreducible generator forces every irreducible polynomial of the same root order to have full support, including factors associated with different constacyclic constants. This yields a uniform gcd and norm obstruction. We develop its short-multiplier extension, give a prime-order cubic family, and establish an explicit quadratic-residue exclusion without a prime-square alphabet or a near-square length hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhu, Hongfeng Wu

item.title: Spatial Token Interleaving and Two-Pass BP Decoding for Semantic Image Transmission
item.description: arXiv:2611.00697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic error control coding (SECC) can correct the residual errors of a standard channel code with a foundation model that supplies a prior on the source content, but existing SECC schemes are designed for text. In this paper, we develop SECC for image transmission with spatial token interleaving and a two-pass belief propagation (BP) schedule. At the transmitter, a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer converts an image into tokens, which are transmitted in multiple low-density parity-check (LDPC) code blocks of fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR). In raster order, a block that BP fails to decode corrupts consecutive token rows, so the interleaver reorders the tokens such that adjacent tokens are carried by different blocks, without additional transmitted bits. At the receiver, after the first BP pass, token recovery fuses the token probabilities given by BP with the predictions of the autoregressive model Emu3-Gen, and the second BP pass decodes each block again with the fused distributions as priors on the information bits. On Kodak24 at 0.5 channel uses per pixel and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 0.15 dB, the second pass removes 92% of the token errors left by token recovery, and interleaving reduces the final token error rate by 88%. At medium to high SNR, the proposed receiver exceeds deep joint source--channel coding baselines with the same channel uses by at least 1.2 dB in peak signal-to-noise ratio.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Feng, Chentao Yue, Haiyao Yu, Gaoyang Pang, Xinyu Chen, Hao Chang, Branka Vucetic, Yonghui Li

item.title: Noise Stability on the Hypercube: Order $7/8$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a balanced Boolean function $f$ on the discrete hypercube, we study the $\alpha$-stability $\mathbb{E}[(T_\rho f)^\alpha]$, where $T_\rho$ is the Boolean noise operator and $0<\alpha<1$. Using the asymmetric Hellinger kernel estimates recently established by OpenAI, we prove that dictators minimize the $7/8$-stability in every dimension and at every correlation $0\le\rho\le1$. At interior correlations they are the only minimizers. As a consequence, dictators minimize the $\alpha$-stability for every $7/8\le\alpha<1$, maximize the $\alpha$-stability for every $1<\alpha<2$, and maximize the one-sided Shannon entropy stability $\mathbb{E}[T_\rho f\log T_\rho f]$. This resolves a conjecture of Li and M\'edard and strengthens the Courtade--Kumar conjecture in the balanced setting.
item.dc:creator: Lei Yu

item.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Mixture Representations of d-Dimensional Triangulated Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.00922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a Gaussian Mixture (GM) representation of a full-dimensional subset of Euclidean space with finite volume from a finite simplicial triangulation in closed form. On each simplex, we replace the uniform probability density function (PDF) with a Gaussian PDF that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence, arriving at the information projection onto the family of Gaussian PDFs. By exploiting affine isomorphisms between simplices, the joint convexity and bijection invariance properties of the KL divergence, identities for Dirichlet PDFs, and a partition-of-unity argument, we establish a dimension-dependent but geometry-independent sharp upper bound on the global KL divergence between the resulting GM PDF and the uniform PDF on the original domain. Numerical examples illustrate the construction and demonstrate its potential in practical applications.
item.dc:creator: Ali Darijani, Benedikt Stratmann, Uwe D. Hanebeck, Ratan Bahadur Thapa, J\"urgen Beyerer, Nehal Afifi

item.title: A density theorem for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.00925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a fixed-characteristic density form of the Berger-Charpin conjecture for non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes: for each prime $p$, the lengths admitting such a non-standard code over some finite field of characteristic $p$ have natural density zero. Thus, for almost every length coprime to $p$, every such code over every finite field of characteristic $p$ has only the permutation automorphisms generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius map. The proof uses the Feng--Hollmann--Li--Xiang classification for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes, a normal form for the deriving constructions in that paper, and a theorem by Wiertelak on multiplicative orders, in the form recalled by Moree.
item.dc:creator: Tao Feng, Henk D. L. Hollmann, Weicong Li, Qing Xiang

item.title: Shared Randomness and Parallel Rounds in Permutation Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.01028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the shared randomness needed to sample a uniform permutation in parallel output rounds. Coordinates committed in the same round are independent conditional on the complete history and the current shared choice. Previous outputs are public; local computation and private randomness are free. We charge each shared choice by the logarithm of its conditional support size and sum these costs along the worst execution path. At every fixed round density $\rho\in(0,1)$, the optimal limiting total-variation error under any $o(n)$ shared budget matches the conditional-marginal optimum, even with arbitrary local kernels and adaptive coordination. A fixed improvement requires linear cost. For exact sampling in $R=\Theta(n)$ rounds, the optimum is $n\Phi(R/n)+O(\log n)$, where $\Phi$ linearly interpolates $\Phi(1/q)=\log q$. A protocol attaining this rate uses an initial seed and at most one further binary shared choice. When $\lceil n/2\rceil\le R\le n$, the finite optimum is $\log\binom{2(n-R)}{n-R}$, attained by an initial seed alone. The approximate converse uses an entropy inequality for sparse injections to control overlap with the target. The exact construction reuses randomness retained in a shared label partition after the first-stage outputs are exposed.
item.dc:creator: Haoxiang Huang

item.title: Maximal input entropy for binary two-deletion and two-insertion channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.01064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under uniform transmission, we determine the received binary words that maximize input entropy for two-deletion and two-insertion channels. For two deletions the maximizers are exactly the two alternating words at every positive received length. For two insertions the same conclusion holds from received length five onward; we give all smaller cases and exact maximal values. The proof combines an embedding-count identity organized by runs with strict convexity estimates, and a grouping of two-position deletion masks. For every insertion radius we give the complete positive embedding histogram of an alternating received word. We also determine its three-deletion histogram for every length, and certify all three-deletion maximizers through received length twelve and all three-insertion maximizers through length eighteen by exact integer comparison. These computations give precise three-error conjectures with their small-length exceptions.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: Digital Twin-Assisted Fast Beam Alignment for mmWave MIMO Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.01107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication relies on directional beam sweeping for initial access, which incurs substantial latency and signaling overhead as antenna arrays grow large and deployments become denser. Machine-learning-based beam prediction can reduce this overhead, but its effectiveness depends on training data that accurately reflects the deployment environment, a requirement that is difficult to meet in practice. This paper presents a latency-aware beam management architecture that integrates digital-twin-assisted prediction, regionbased localization, weighted ensemble learning, and explainability-driven beam pruning into a unified framework. A digital twin (DT) generates site-specific ray-traced channel knowledge offline, enabling environment-aware beam prediction without exhaustive real-world measurements and supporting both initial access and beam tracking. The proposed ensemble learning scheme combines a base classifier and a specialist classifier through reliability-weighted fusion to improve prediction accuracy and robustness, while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based attribution pruning reduces the beam codebook to a small subset of the most informative beams for beam allocation. To capture the distributional mismatch between the DT and real-world environments: the network was trained on imperfect digital-twin data but evaluated on real-world surrobase data. Results show that the proposed method achieves 96.80% top-1 and 98.36% top-3 beam prediction accuracy, while reducing over-the-air sounding overhead by nearly an order of magnitude relative to exhaustive sweeping, outperforming convolutional and deep neural network baselines from prior work.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Kamran Saeed, Ashfaq Khokhar

item.title: Sub Terahertz LEO Satellite Communication: Is Doppler Shift a Major Challenge?
item.description: arXiv:2611.01264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the impact of Doppler frequency shift on sub-terahertz low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications using OFDM transmission. To comprehensively evaluate the severity of the Doppler shift impact on sub-terahertz satellite-to-ground links, we first put together an evaluation framework that jointly accounts for major Doppler-induced and non-Doppler-induced signal impairments in such systems. We then compare and contrast three possible engineering approaches to deal with Doppler shift in such a communication system. Our study concludes that (i)~while just ignoring the Doppler effect in such high-frequency and high-mobility systems substantially compromises the performance and reliability, (ii)~most of the negative effects can be eliminated by implementing only a small set of low-complexity measures. We particularly show that even a single Doppler shift estimation over a 5-min-long satellite pass over the ground user location may be sufficient to ensure high performance throughout the entire connectivity period. Hence, while Doppler shift is an important effect to account for in sub-terahertz LEO satellite communications, it should not constitute a critical design challenge for these emerging systems.
item.dc:creator: Seongjoon Kang, Parisa Ramezani, Ki Won Sung, Vitaly Petrov

item.title: Polynomial-Time Minimax Prediction for Stationary Renewal Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The minimax next-symbol Kullback-Leibler risk for stationary binary renewal processes is known to have order n^(-1/2). We give a polynomial-time predictor attaining this order for an arbitrary unknown finite-mean interarrival law. The construction uses a classical type-uniform renewal code. Its contribution is an exact dynamic program for censored prefix marginals, avoiding enumeration of gap histograms or binary completions. Combined with an established prediction reduction, it gives risk at most [log M_(n+1)+log(n+2)]/n, where M_N counts renewal types. Shared suffix updates reduce the total computation to O(n^3) arithmetic work and polynomial bit complexity, without tail, mixing, known-mean, or bounded-support assumptions. The statistical rate and its lower bound are prior results; the proposed advance concerns computation.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Chen, Yiming Ma

item.title: Secrecy Sum-Rate Maximization for RSMA-Enabled Pinching-Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates secrecy sum-rate (SSR) maximization in a downlink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-enabled single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) with an external eavesdropper. The RSMA power allocation, secure common-rate allocation, and pinching-antenna (PA) positions are jointly optimized subject to transmit-power, per-user secrecy-rate, and PA-placement constraints. To tackle the resulting nonconvex problem, an alternating-optimization framework is developed, combining successive convex approximation for RSMA resource allocation with feasibility-preserving projected gradient ascent for PA-position optimization. Numerical results show that the proposed design consistently outperforms the considered benchmarks in terms of average SSR, demonstrating the benefits of joint RSMA resource and PA-position optimization for secure PASS transmission.
item.dc:creator: Code Kebe, Saeid Pakravan, Wessam Ajib

item.title: MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Square-Root Length on Hyperelliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.01546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every fixed genus $g\geq2$ and every $0<\rho<1$, we construct maximum distance separable (MDS) algebraic geometry codes over $\F_q$ for all sufficiently large odd squares $q$. Their parameters are $\bigl[n,\lfloor\rho n\rfloor,n-\lfloor\rho n\rfloor+1\bigr]_q$ with $n=\sqrt q+1+O_g(q^{1/4})$. The codes use full Riemann--Roch spaces on genus-$g$ hyperelliptic curves. They are not monomially equivalent to generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) codes when $q$ is sufficiently large. An infinite subfamily has exact length $n=\sqrt q+2gq^{1/4}+1$.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Guorui Ma

item.title: Second-Order Asymptotics for the Scalar Gaussian Broadcast Channel
item.description: arXiv:2611.01583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper characterizes the second-order coding region of the scalar Gaussian broadcast channel along the curved boundary of its capacity region. The characterization holds under both average and maximal error criteria and allows correlation between the receiver noises. At each interior point of this boundary, the second-order region is a halfspace, as in the work of Scarlett and the author on Gaussian multiple-access channels with degraded message sets. Achievability follows from spherical superposition coding with a blocklength-dependent power allocation. The main innovation lies in the converse. Using Ornstein--Uhlenbeck entropy dissipation and Gaussian functional inequalities, we construct an auxiliary observation through an additive Gaussian noise channel and establish quantitative relative entropy bounds for the channel output distributions conditioned on this observation. The strong functional representation lemma of Li and El Gamal then allows us to select a realization of its independent random seed to obtain a deterministic partition of the retained receiver-1 message set. The component label plays a role analogous to the auxiliary random variable in the capacity characterization, while providing the distributional control needed at the second-order scale. These properties guide the construction of auxiliary output measures whose likelihood ratios admit the cancellations and normal approximation needed to evaluate an information spectrum converse.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Y. F. Tan

item.title: 6G Uplink Waveform and Rank Selection under Distributed Reception
item.description: arXiv:2611.01590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The development of 6G uplink is expanding waveform and spatial transmission options, while distributed reception makes their relative merits depend on the spatial and frequency structure of the aggregate channel. We study the joint selection of cyclic prefix orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing and discrete Fourier transform spread OFDM at rank 1 and noncoherent rank 2 under common user equipment power constraints and centralized linear minimum mean-square error reception. We derive waveform switching thresholds at both ranks and a rank selection margin, establishing conditions for selecting among the four modes based on available transmit power, DFT despreading loss, and spatial multiplexing gain. We then characterize how port gains and correlations at individual access points (APs) form aggregate spatial separation and influence mode selection. At fixed port gains and available transmit powers, improving spatial separation without reducing it on any subcarrier increases the rank selection margin, while its effect on the preferred waveform within rank 2 depends on the frequency distribution of the improvement. Numerical results show that different AP deployments can favor different waveforms and ranks, even with the same receive antenna budget and comparable aggregate channel gains, including waveform switches at a fixed preferred rank.
item.dc:creator: Yewen Cao, Fen Hou, Yulin Shao

item.title: Worst-User Outage Probability Minimization in Active RIS-Aided Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a worst-user outage probability minimization problem in active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided systems is addressed. Since the resulting problem involves a discontinuous objective function over an unknown channel distribution, a sequence of reformulations is applied by integrating a probability-simplex user weighting, a softplus surrogate for differentiability, and entropic tail-risk aggregation for rare but severe outage events. Based on the reformulated problem, a data-driven stochastic optimization technique that relies on historical channel samples is adopted to jointly optimize the beamformer and reflection coefficients with projected adaptive moment estimation. Simulation results show advantages of the proposed technique for reliability-oriented active RIS transmission design.
item.dc:creator: Donghwan Shin, Hyeongtaek Lee, Junil Choi

item.title: How Much Does Random Rotation Help GPTQ? Sharp Worst-Case Rate Gaps in the High-Rate Regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.01669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GPTQ is Babai's nearest-plane algorithm on the lattice of the Cholesky factor of the layer's input second moment $\Sigma$. In the high-rate, entropy-coded regime it needs $\tfrac12\log_2(\AM/\GM)$ of its Cholesky pivots more bits than WaterSIC, which is within $0.255$ bit of the rate-distortion limit for every $\Sigma$; random rotations close most of this gap in practice, and Ordentlich and Polyanskiy asked for the worst-case gap between rotated GPTQ and WaterSIC. We show that after a Haar rotation the $k$-th pivot converges almost surely, uniformly in $k\ge\delta n$ and over spectra $\nu$ of bounded condition number, to $1/S_\nu(-k/n)$, a classical formula from the theory of Lyapunov exponents, and use it to answer the question. Over spectra with condition number $\kappa$ the worst rotated gap is $\tfrac12\log_2\kappa-\log_2\ln\kappa+\tfrac12-\tfrac1{\ln2}+o(1)$ bits, attained only by two-point spectra, just $\tfrac12\log_2\ln\kappa+O(1)$ bits below the worst case without rotation, so rotation cannot replace waterfilling in general. It nearly can on real layers: rotation cuts the cost of an $\eta$-fraction of outlier eigenvalues of size $\mu$ from about $\eta\mu$ to $\eta^2\mu/2$ to leading order, but cannot remove spectral spread on a logarithmic scale; for non-Gaussian weights it also adds a weight-side rate cost, which we characterize exactly under a standard high-rate assumption. On $96$ Hessians of Qwen3 and Llama-3.1 the rotated gap has median $0.04$ bit and maximum $0.36$ bit, against $2$--$5$ bits in the worst case for the same condition numbers, and the limit matches it to within $0.009$ bit.
item.dc:creator: Runguo Li

item.title: Communication with Adversarial Users: Byzantine Models in Multi-User Information Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.01678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider communication systems operating in environments where some participating users cannot be trusted. This motivates the study of Byzantine communication models, in which users may behave adversarially. In this survey, we provide a unified information-theoretic perspective on communication with adversarial users in multi-user settings. We review recent advances in Byzantine multiple access channels, including reliable communication, adversary identification, and distributed function computation. Furthermore, we discuss extensions to classical-quantum channels and highlight fundamental differences between classical and quantum models. Finally, we outline key open problems and future research directions at the intersection of communication, computation, and security.
item.dc:creator: Minglai Cai, Christian Deppe, Neha Sangwan

item.title: Instance-Specific Sharp Convergence Rate of the Add-$\lambda$ Estimator via Feature Space Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.01828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the Feature Space Decomposition framework, we establish non-asymptotic matching upper and lower bounds for the expected Kullback-Leibler estimation error of the Add-$\lambda$ estimator of a discrete probability distribution, for any signal, any dimension, any sample size, and any $\lambda>0$.
item.dc:creator: Zong Shang

item.title: Wideband Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC) for Frequency-Flat and Frequency-Selective Processing
item.description: arXiv:2611.02109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC) has been proposed as an analog processing architecture to perform efficient computation in the microwave domain. Consisting of reconfigurable impedance networks, a MiLAC can extract many of the gains of large multi-antenna systems without costly digital processing, e.g., achieving capacity in narrowband multiple-input single-output (MISO). However, the behavior of wideband MiLAC, required to support high data-rate transmissions, is widely unknown. The impedance components of MiLACs have non-trivial frequency-dependent response, requiring specific implementations to characterize it. In this work, we consider MiLAC implementations based on LC resonators with tunable capacitance, which allow synthesizing near-arbitrary passive lossless impedance matrices at individual frequencies using inductors and varactors. We characterize the mapping between optimal MISO precoding at a reference frequency, and the vector of capacitances configuring the MiLAC. We derive the degrees of freedom (DoFs) remaining after fixing such optimum precoding at the reference frequency, and show that these DoFs can be exploited to tune the frequency response of the MiLAC. We propose two techniques to exploit these DoFs: a closed-form approach for frequency-flat MiLAC processing, and a numerical approach for multi-frequency MiLAC processing, optimizing processing at frequencies other than the reference one. The frequency-flat approach shows satisfactory performance in a simulated frequency-flat millimeter-wave scenario, approaching the performance of digital processing. The multi-frequency approach can adapt to the frequency-selectivity of a simulated sub-6GHz scenario, attaining gains over frequency-flat digital processing. This constitutes the first demonstration that realistic MiLAC implementations can be configured to perform independent computations at different frequencies.
item.dc:creator: Juan Vidal Alegr\'{i}a, Matteo Nerini, Bruno Clerckx

item.title: Concatenation Locality under Successive Adjacent Transpositions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study codes correcting up to $t\geq1$ successive adjacent transpositions, using block concatenation to support blockwise encoding and decoding. A fixed set $P$ of words of length $b$ over a $q$-symbol alphabet generates, for every $m$, the length-$mb$ code of all concatenations of $m$ words from $P$. For our explicit constructions, the prepared encoder and decoder depend only on the block parameters and are reused at every concatenation length. We first prove that correction at every concatenation length is certified by a single finite test at $2t+1$ blocks, and this test is tight over a $q$-symbol alphabet exactly when $\binom q2\geq2t$. For binary words and $b\geq2t+1$, we give an explicit construction with total redundancy at most $mt\log_2 b+O_t(m)$, matching the optimal per-block redundancy $t\log_2 b+O_t(1)$ among block sets correcting at every concatenation length. Among all binary $t$-correcting codes of length $mb$, the optimal total redundancy is $t\log_2(mb)+O_t(1)$. Using all concatenations of one block set makes our total redundancy grow linearly in $m$ and buys independent block encoding, with one encoder and decoder at every length. The construction encodes and decodes in time linear in $mb$ for fixed $b,t$, and recovers the $j$-th source block from the first $jb$ received symbols. We also prove that, whenever the length-$mb$ code corrects $t$ transpositions, the $j$-th source block is determined within $2tb$ received symbols beyond position $jb$, and that explicit binary block sets with rates tending to one as $b$ grows with $t$ fixed attain this bound in the worst case. Finally, we prove that every ordinary correcting code contains a constant fraction of its words whose arbitrary concatenations retain correction, for fixed $q,t$.
item.dc:creator: Adelin Ataba (Yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

item.title: Achievability of CSS codes performance limits over Pauli channels under separate ML decoding with bounded graphical complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.02339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Capacity-approaching quantum error correction faces a fundamental tension: the required parity-check matrices need to become increasingly dense, while practical decoding and syndrome extraction favor sparse, bounded-degree structures. Reconciling these competing requirements remains an important open problem in quantum code design. We construct Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code ensembles that approach the CSS rate over memoryless Pauli channels under maximum-likelihood decoding while retaining sparse, bounded-degree graphical representations. The construction separates parity-check density from graphical complexity: although capacity-approaching components may require dense parity-check matrices, they are represented by sparse concatenated factor graphs. We first study a construction combining low-density parity-check (LDPC) and low-density generator-matrix (LDGM) component codes and numerically analyze the average weight distributions of the resulting codes. Motivated by these results, we introduce a second construction based on concatenated LDPC and LDGM codes and generalized irregular repeat-accumulate (GIRA) codes. We derive bounds on the average weight distribution of the resulting sum ensemble and use the Miller-Burshtein framework to prove simultaneous reliability of the two CSS decoding components. Consequently, the proposed ensemble achieves rates arbitrarily close to the CSS hashing bound under separate bit- and phase-error correction, while maintaining bounded graphical complexity, thus providing a foundation for future iterative decoders and indirect syndrome-extraction architectures.
item.dc:creator: Gulnihal Mercanoglu, Achilleas Anastasopoulos, S. Sandeep Pradhan

item.title: A Sharp Mutual Information Bound for Binary Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a sharp upper bound on the mutual information between two binary random variables in terms of their distribution-dependent KL contraction coefficient. This resolves the binary-pair conjecture of Anantharam, Gohari, Kamath, and Nair. Equality holds if and only if the variables are independent or form a doubly symmetric binary source. The proof uses supporting tangents of an entropy curve to vary the input distribution and the channel while preserving the contraction coefficient. Together with tensorization and data processing, the result also bounds the mutual information between binary outputs obtained separately from two correlated observation sequences. When the observation pairs are independent copies of a finite-alphabet pair, this bound depends only on the law of one pair and not on the number of observations.
item.dc:creator: Qianmian Guo

item.title: Inverse Design of Finite-State Channels by Dynamic Measure Matching
item.description: arXiv:2611.02400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the optimization approach to biology, we formulate an inverse problem for communication with memory: construct a finite-state channel for which a given signaling behavior supports capacity-achieving codes. Dynamic measure matching is introduced to turn a directed-information converse into conditions on the channel dynamics. These conditions lead to a new notion of dynamic surprise: the log ratio of physical to test output probabilities with a continuation correction for future signaling opportunities. The matching inequalities bound its conditional mean. For fixed architecture, test law, and potential, channel row synthesis under convex physical restrictions is convex. For every signaling constraint represented by a finite irreducible constrained graph of positive entropy, we construct a channel law under which undesired inputs remain available and behaviorally distinct while incurring a strict information penalty. A noisy refractory family has an exact capacity plateau, followed by an interval in which Shannon and zero-error feedback capacities differ. Explicit zero-error codes attain capacity in the graph construction and on the plateau. In this family, a Gibbs choice maximizes the penalty and makes dynamic surprise equal its conditional mean on every transition, yielding an exact trajectory-wise likelihood identity, a finite-block bound on successful decoding with premature requests, and an exponential strong converse. An exact gap decomposition into action residuals and output-law divergence constrains every reliable capacity-approaching code. Within the strict plateau, positive discrimination exponents for unused dynamics require a positive rate loss, while sparse probing permits consistent estimation at asymptotic capacity. A chemical channel illustrates how premature stimulation can alter future responsiveness while leaving the immediate output law unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Lav R. Varshney

item.title: Finding optimal measurement sequences for broken or constrained measuring devices
item.description: arXiv:2611.02470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measuring devices do not always function perfectly due to fatigue, damage, or malfunction. When device repair or replacement is not possible, it becomes necessary to seek optimal measurements from a broken device. We show this is possible via a sequential decision making process where we optimize measurement sequences over the remaining available measurements using information theory. With dynamic programming, we show greedy measurement sequences are always suboptimal for a simple class of measurement constraints. Greedy measurement sequences generally lead to equiprobable measurement outcomes, while the optimal policy is found to select each measurement in such a way as to assign a low probability to any measurement outcome that triggers a constraint condition; leading to measurement outcomes that are not equiprobable. A measurement sequence generated under this policy is shown to decompress its source: that is, the expected number of measurement outcomes is strictly greater than the number of bits it encodes, defining a key property of constrained measurements. Dynamic programming is inefficient for finding optimal measurement sequences, so we develop an alternative algorithm related to optimal binary decision trees. By deriving upper and lower complexity bounds for the task, we propose this algorithm as an efficient means to find optimal measurements for a broken or constrained measuring device.
item.dc:creator: Peter N. Loxley

item.title: Information Complexity of Inner Product and Matrix Multiplication via Shannon-to-Min-Entropy Conversion
item.description: arXiv:2611.02684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the information complexity of matrix multiplication over finite fields under independent uniform inputs, up to a universal additive constant. The binary inner-product case resolves the open question of Braverman, Garg, Pankratov, and Weinstein on the optimal dependence of information complexity on the error probability. For inputs in $\mathbb F_2^m$ and error at most $\varepsilon\in[0,1/2]$, the information complexity with output at Bob lies between $(1-2\varepsilon)m-c_0$ and $(1-2\varepsilon)m$, where $c_0<4.772$ is a universal constant. For independent uniform matrices $X\in\mathbb F_q^{t\times m}$ and $Y\in\mathbb F_q^{s\times m}$, where $t\le s$, computing $XY^{\mathsf T}$ with output at Bob and error at most $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ has information complexity $(1-q^{ts}\varepsilon/(q^{ts}-1))^+mt\log_2q$, up to an additive gap of less than $9.544$ bits. This gap is independent of the matrix dimensions, field size, and error. At zero error, the information complexity is exactly $mt\log_2q$. The information lower bounds for both inner product and matrix multiplication follow from a new Shannon-to-min-entropy theorem for convolution on discrete groups. Let $Q_1,\ldots,Q_k$ be the finitely supported distributions of independent random variables taking values in a discrete group, and let $s$ be the largest support size. We show that if $k\ge\lceil\lfloor\log_2s\rfloor\ln2\rceil$, then the min-entropy of their ordered product is at least the average Shannon entropy of the $Q_i$ minus $c_0$ bits. This holds for arbitrary discrete groups, including infinite and noncommutative groups, even when the input distributions differ. The leading coefficient of the logarithmic threshold is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Xiaohong Cai, Mingyang Zhu

item.title: Design and Analysis of Pinching-Antenna Systems With Radially Deployed Waveguides (X-PASS)
item.description: arXiv:2611.02687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) reconfigure the wireless channel by positioning dielectric antennas along a waveguide. A single waveguide, however, confines its antennas to one line, so that good coverage of an area has relied on several waveguides or waveguide segments with separate feeds. This paper proposes X-PASS, in which a hub feeds radially deployed waveguide arms, one pinching antenna on each, and drives them by arm selection, aggregation or multiplexing. It models the hub with its insertion losses, derives a unified signal-to-noise ratio expression for these three operating modes, and derives in closed form a radius inside which aggregation outperforms selection. Numerical results validate the analysis and compare the coverage of X-PASS with that of the other layouts at equal transmit power.
item.dc:creator: Wei Jiang, Hans D. Schotten

item.title: Movable Antenna-Assisted Secret Key Generation over Temporally Correlated Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.02761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical-layer key generation (PLKG) exploits reciprocal channel dynamics to generate symmetric keys, addressing the key distribution problem in wireless communications. However, strong temporal correlation in slow-fading environments limits fresh randomness and results in low key generation rates. Movable antennas (MAs) introduce spatial degrees of freedom through antenna repositioning, providing a new approach to addressing the limitation. This paper investigates MA-assisted PLKG over temporally correlated channels. A first-order Gauss-Markov process is utilized to characterize the temporal correlation of multipath gains. We characterize the full-sequence mutual information (MI) over temporally correlated channels. For fixed antenna positions and beamforming, we establish a finite-horizon approximation error bound that vanishes as both effective signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) increase. We derive a closed-form expression for the one-step conditional MI and adopt it as a tractable key-information metric. A nonconvex problem is formulated to jointly optimize antenna positions and per-slot beamforming under transmit-power and minimum-spacing constraints. We develop an alternating optimization algorithm, combining an exact principal-eigenvector beamforming solution with feasible SCA-based projected gradient position updates. Simulation results demonstrate that the MA-assisted scheme outperforms the fixed-position antenna baseline. At a high temporal correlation coefficient, position optimization achieves approximately $51\%$ higher rates than fixed antennas. Joint position and beamforming optimization provides a further $106\%$ gain over position optimization alone, demonstrating more pronounced gains under strong temporal correlation.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyu Huang, Chen Sun, Guyue Li, Guanghui Wen, Xianbin Wang

item.title: Localization MSE Analysis for Cooperative OFDM-ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2611.02783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a receiver-specific mean-squared-error (MSE) framework for cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) localization using random orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) payloads. It captures local peak perturbations and incorrect ambiguity-peak acquisition for two classical receiver processing schemes: matched filtering (MF) and reciprocal filtering (RF). For scatterers well separated in delay, we quantify how frequency spread and interference induced by symbol-energy fluctuations affect local delay errors under MF. RF removes symbol-dependent weighting but amplifies noise for low-energy symbols. Payload-conditioned joint Gaussian delay profiles yield peak-selection probabilities, which combine with nonlinear multistatic fusion errors to approximate position MSE while accounting for network geometry. Numerical results illustrate receiver-dependent estimation errors and the benefits of frequency-dependent constellation allocation.
item.dc:creator: Kaitao Meng, Kawon Han, Christos Masouros

item.title: Customizing Wireless Channels via Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces: Feasibility, Fundamental Limits, and Constructive Design
item.description: arXiv:2611.02894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By adjusting their reflection coefficients, intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) can reshape the channels between a base station (BS) and user equipment (UE). Existing studies mainly optimize IRS phase-shifts for communication objectives, leaving the physical attainability of prescribed IRS-reflected channels largely unexplored. This paper investigates channel customization with a phase-only IRS under three progressively relaxed criteria. Observing that the customization mean-squared error (MSE) has the same mathematical form as the signal MSE of a point-to-point multiple-input multiple-output system, we construct a counterpart problem to characterize individual singular-coordinate gain limits and the condition for attaining the amplitude-matching upper bound. To address multi-stream phase conflicts, we analyze principal contribution area (PCA) overlap and derive sufficient array-size conditions for disjoint PCAs under a specified focused-vector construction with parallel uniform linear arrays. We also derive necessary conditions from the two propagation links' singular values and an array-size restriction under the parallel-array Fresnel model. Both the restriction and the construction involve the BS--IRS array-size product. Numerical results show that jointly selecting right singular vectors and IRS phase-shifts reduces mean customization MSE, whereas gains exceeding propagation spectral limits cannot be realized exactly. These results provide design guidance and highlight spectral limits of phase-only IRS channel customization.
item.dc:creator: Xiyuan Liu, Qingqing Wu, Guangji Chen, Yuxuan Chen, Wen Chen

item.title: Fluid Antenna Array-Enabled Near-Field ISAC: Joint Port Position Optimization and Transmit Beamforming Design
item.description: arXiv:2611.03000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) have shown that activating a single port from a densely packed antenna array can yield spatial diversity comparable to that of tens of independent antennas, a property that has substantially improved communication reliability and efficiency. The fluid antenna array (FAA) extends this concept to multi-port configurations while avoiding complex multi-dimensional spatial correlation, and offers significant geometrical flexibility under a finite aperture and a limited port budget. These attributes motivate environment-adaptive array geometry for sensing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Although this flexibility enables adaptive array geometries that exploit near-field distance-angle information, improving multi-parameter target estimation under communication and deployment constraints remains challenging. In this paper, we propose a planar FAA-assisted near-field ISAC framework for multiuser communication and target sensing. Specifically, we derive the Fisher information matrix (FIM) and the corresponding Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB) for the joint estimation of target range, zenith angle, azimuth angle, and radial velocity. Based on the derived CRB, we jointly optimize the FAA port positions and transmit beamforming to improve sensing accuracy while satisfying communication signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), transmit power, and physical deployment constraints. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a two-stage alternating optimization algorithm, in which transmit beamforming is optimized through semidefinite relaxation (SDR), while FAA port positions are successively optimized through discrete search and continuous refinement. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm achieves favorable sensing performance while maintaining a reasonable computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Wangqi Shi, Zhentian Zhang, Hao Jiang, Zaichen Zhang, Kin-Fai Tong

item.title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Uncoded versus Row-Wise Coded Placements
item.description: arXiv:2611.03045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A\leq K$ users is active in the delivery phase. In all regimes where the optimal hotplug tradeoff is known, it depends only on $A$, not on $K$; whether this holds in general is open. We show that: (i) Under uncoded placement, YMA delivery with MAN placement, where offline users are assigned the demands of active users, is optimal. Hence, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, while the MAN placement is optimal for every number of active users; (ii) Under row-wise placement (RWP), where each cache is a function of the user's own row of each file, every classical scheme can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code. The resulting hotplug scheme has the tradeoff of the classical model with $A$ users, for every $A\leq K$: there is no load penalty, but the placement depends on $K$. We then derive a converse for RWP, which shows that: (a) for $2\leq N\leq A$, the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV) is RWP optimal for $AM\leq N/(N-1)$, which settles the RWP tradeoff for $N=2$; (b) YMA is RWP optimal at $AM=N$; and (c) for $N=A=3$, GV is RWP optimal for $M\leq 1$. Hence, the Reed-Solomon embeddings of these schemes are optimal among embedded RWP schemes.
item.dc:creator: Daniela Tuninetti

item.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for BD-RIS-Assisted Multi-UAV RSMA Communications
item.description: arXiv:2611.03047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) extend conventional diagonal RISs by allowing controllable coupling among reflecting elements. This flexibility is attractive for aerial networks, where unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) face rapidly varying channels and strict power limits. In this paper, we study a hybrid BD-RIS-assisted multi-UAV rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlink, in which UAVs within favourable BD-RIS coverage use both direct and BD-RIS-aided links, whereas the remaining UAVs are served through direct links only. We formulate a network sum-rate maximization problem that jointly optimizes UAV trajectories, RSMA common-rate allocation, beamforming, BD-RIS scattering matrices, and UAV-BD-RIS association. The resulting mixed-integer non-convex problem is solved by using deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, equipped with a constraint-preserving action layer that generates reciprocal and lossless BD-RIS responses in closed form and handles the binary association inside the environment transition. Simulation results, averaged over three training seeds under a physically consistent channel model with blocked direct links near the BD-RISs, show that the proposed design attains a sum rate comparable to SAC and higher than twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient ( TD3), proximal policy optimization (PPO), and deep Q-network (DQN), exceeds per-slot alternating optimization with fixed trajectories at about 1/65 of its per-slot runtime, and benefits mainly from RSMA, while the additional BD-RIS gain is modest.
item.dc:creator: Aamer Mohamed Huroon, Ali A. Nasir, Daniel B. da Costa

item.title: Reed-Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs
item.description: arXiv:2611.03145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that any linear $3$-query locally correctable code $C \colon \mathbb{F}_2^k \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with constant correction radius must have length $n \geq 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{k})}$. This improves on the prior best lower bound of $2^{\Omega(\sqrt{k/\log k})}$, due to [AG24], and shows that the folklore construction of linear $3$-LCCs from Reed-Muller codes, which achieve length $n = 2^{O(\sqrt{k})}$, is optimal up to constant factors in the exponent. Our proof builds on the approach of [KM24a], further refined in [Yan24,KM24b], that uses "chain derived equations" in combination with Kikuchi graphs. The crux of our argument is to show that a certain edge-coloured Kikuchi graph has a unique colour cycle: a cycle in which some colour is used exactly once. We do this by controlling the distribution of colours at each vertex in the graph using a random walk mixing argument and a novel hypergraph decomposition based on edge expansion of the hypergraph's "flattening" into a graph.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Janzer, Peter Manohar

item.title: The Covering Radius of the Reed--Muller Code \texorpdfstring{$\RM(3,8)$}{RM(3,8)} is 56
item.description: arXiv:2611.03186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the covering radius of the third-order Reed--Muller code in eight variables is fifty-six. The proof separates even- and odd-weight inputs by moment-controlled slicing. On the even side, a transport invariant on quadratic-label stars and consistency of singleton restrictions give a compatible cubic correction. On the odd side, symmetry of the third moment yields a covariance-rank obstruction. Its rank-two exception is a quartic plus three points of a two-plane; the zero-second-moment case is a prescribed-point perturbation of a quintic. We prove that every such point perturbation has third-order nonlinearity at most fifty-five by a marked derivative identity and complete restriction-code covers. Consequently the maximum among exact-degree-eight functions is fifty-five. The structural reductions are proved analytically, and complete finite certificates verify the explicitly stated local covering and compatibility assertions. The matching lower bound follows from the published quartic relative radius.
item.dc:creator: Zhihang Zhao, Yansheng Wu

item.title: Harnessing Mutual Coupling in Cell-Free mMIMO
item.description: arXiv:2611.03193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter investigates a cell-free massive MIMO system with $L$ access points (APs), each employing a small fixed-form-factor, uniform linear array of $N$ potentially closely spaced antennas. Utilizing multiport communication theory, we analyze the impact of mutual coupling on uplink and downlink spectral efficiency (SE) under various impedance-matching strategies. We compare two deployment regimes: ($i$) increasing $N$ while $L$ is kept fixed, and ($ii$) increasing $N$ while fixing the total antenna count $M = NL$. Numerical results show that, with a full matching network, mutual coupling itself becomes beneficial when an AP serves several user equipments, which is the typical operating regime of user-centric cell-free networks. Furthermore, with full matching, antenna densification can enhance SE or allow for a reduction in the number of APs without performance loss. Since full matching networks remain of manageable size in the small arrays of distributed APs, unlike in large centralized arrays, cell-free networks offer a natural setting for exploiting mutual coupling.
item.dc:creator: Erind Tufa, Antonio A. D'Amico, Luca Sanguinetti

item.title: Good rational functions up to degree six
item.description: arXiv:2611.03368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Locally recoverable codes (LRCs) are fundamental to the architecture of modern distributed storage systems. The Tamo-Barg construction of optimal LRCs was revolutionized by the introduction of good polynomials, which group evaluation points into local recovery sets. However, polynomial constructions are constrained by their inherently large Galois groups, which limit the number of totally split rational places. Recent advances have generalized this paradigm to good rational functions, which leverage the geometry of the projective line to achieve minimal Galois groups and subsequently codes with greater length. In this paper, we complete the classification of good rational functions of degree up to $6$ in characteristic $2$. By embedding the problem into algebraic function field theory, we explicitly determine the minimal arithmetic and geometric Galois groups for these low degrees. Furthermore, we move beyond asymptotic Hasse-Weil estimates by proving that the exact number of totally split places over extension fields obeys a linear recurring sequence (LRS). This gives an efficient method for computing the exact lengths and dimensions of the corresponding optimal LRCs and, in many cases, yields parameters beyond those obtainable from good polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Anuvrat Jaindungarwal, Divyesh Vaghasiya

item.title: Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Distributed Consensus: Algorithm Design and Power Control Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.03378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-coherent over-the-air (NCOTA) aggregation offers a scalable and communication-efficient approach to distributed average consensus in wireless networks, without requiring instantaneous channel state information (CSI) or phase alignment. However, persistent aggregation errors pose fundamental challenges in achieving exact average consensus under nominal distributed averaging protocols. In this paper, we develop an NCOTA consensus framework that accommodates row-stochastic mixing, without requiring the conventional average-preservation property of doubly stochastic mixing matrices. Building on a distributed optimization formulation of average consensus, we propose a decentralized projected gradient descent with row-stochastic mixing (DPGD-RS) algorithm and establish its mean-square convergence to the exact average of the agents' initial states. We further derive a closed-form upper bound on the mean-square consensus error, characterizing the effects of aggregation uncertainty, network connectivity, and mixing imbalance. Guided by this analysis, we propose a spectral-reshaping power control (SR-PC) scheme that jointly optimizes transmit powers and receive-scaling factors to accelerate convergence by balancing aggregation accuracy and network mixing. Numerical results validate the theoretical convergence guarantees and demonstrate that the proposed power control scheme significantly accelerates convergence compared with full-power transmission and spectral-radius-minimization benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Yuhang Deng, Zheng Chen, Erik G. Larsson

item.title: Beyond GNSS: Leveraging LEO Satellite Signals of Opportunity for Doppler Positioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.03440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large constellations of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites provide ubiquitous global connectivity; yet, their rapid motion introduces significant Doppler shift effects. While challenging for communication, these effects can be leveraged for precise user terminal (UT) positioning, particularly in GNSS-denied environments where traditional satellite-based navigation struggles. Unlike GNSS, most LEO satellites lack dedicated navigation signals, motivating signals-of-opportunity (SOPs) approaches that repurpose existing LEO signals and use publicly available two-line element (TLE) files for orbital information, although ephemeris errors can limit accuracy. This article explores the fundamental principles, challenges, and enabling technologies for LEO-based Doppler shift positioning, highlighting its advantages over conventional non-Doppler methods, and discussing future research directions. Furthermore, to facilitate realistic and reproducible performance evaluation beyond stochastic modeling, we propose SionnaNTN-RT, a ray tracing framework for non-terrestrial network (NTN) built upon Sionna, enabling end-to-end simulation of Doppler-based positioning. Simulation results demonstrate that Doppler-based positioning can achieve high positioning accuracy in both urban and open-sky environments, highlighting its promise for next-generation positioning systems.
item.dc:creator: Md. Ali Hasan, M. Humayun Kabir, Sangmin Han, Wonjae Shin, H. Vincent Poor

item.title: An information-geometric formulation of distributed computation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how complex systems perform computations, i.e. how they store, transmit, and transform information across their components, is a major goal across the natural sciences. However, characterising genuinely collective computations across multiple inputs and outputs that cannot be reduced to contributions from individual components remains an open problem. In this work, we introduce $\Phi\text{ID}^{IG}$, a geometric theory of information dynamics that captures irreducible collective phenomena and enables a complete decomposition of multi-input multi-output operations into interpretable computational modes, providing a complete informational profile of a system. We first validate our framework to identify and quantify distinct computational modes in discrete and Gaussian systems with known ground truth. We then apply it to uncover the computational architecture of complex systems across synthetic and real-world scenarios, including chaotic maps, where distinct universality classes are associated with characteristic modes of computation; brain anatomy of over 100 mammalian species, revealing an evolutionary shift towards more distributed computation in the human neocortex; and financial markets, where collective computations recover the modular organisation of market sectors. Overall, our results show how complex systems can be quantitatively investigated through multidimensional computational portraits derived from the geometry of their underlying probability distributions.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Liardi, George Blackburne, Pedro A. M. Mediano

item.title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
item.description: arXiv:2611.03558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Nomeir, Sennur Ulukus

item.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.03578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.
item.dc:creator: Keita Ishizuka

item.title: The optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and bounds from Voronoi facets
item.description: arXiv:2611.00100v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The computer-assisted proof combines the classification of secondary cones with integration over Voronoi cells and weighted sums of squares. In dimensions at least two, comparison with circular cones gives a lower bound in terms of the number of Voronoi facets, improving the sphere bound and recovering the hexagonal value in dimension two. We prove Ajjanagadde's circular-cone concavity conjecture and deduce the lattice case of his conjectured quantization bound.
item.dc:creator: Tianle Liu

item.title: Cyclotomic polynomials with trinomial irreducible factors over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.00647v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the pairs $(q,n)$, where $q$ is a prime power, $n>1$, and $\gcd(n,q)=1$, for which every irreducible factor of $\Phi_n(x)$ over $\F_q$ has exactly three nonzero terms. The positive support exponents of these factors have a common greatest common divisor, which gives a unique reduction by a power substitution. The reduced degree is two in odd characteristic and belongs to $\{2,3,4\}$ in characteristic two; the cubic and quartic cases arise by scalar substitution from the layers of orders $7$ and $15$. This yields necessary and sufficient arithmetic conditions on $(q,n)$ and explicit factorizations. Among the classified families, precisely those arising from quartic bases have a divisor layer containing an irreducible factor with more than three terms.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhu

item.title: Leaving Quantum Bias on the Table: Pushforwards as a Path to Quantum Advantage in Constrained Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.00759v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Constrained quantum samplers often produce infeasible outputs that retain information about good feasible solutions. We develop a post-measurement framework that constructs problem-dependent classical feasibility maps from constraint-violation statistics and pushes the raw quantum sampling law forward onto the feasible set. The probability of each repaired solution is the total raw mass of its repair preimage, enlarging the successful sampling event from a target feasible set to its full repair preimage. We derive exact identities for repaired success and expected cost, and separate repair-basin geometry from sampler-dependent probability concentration. For noisy implementations, we distinguish leakage from the encoded subspace from concentration loss within it. For permutation constraints, Hungarian maximum-overlap repair provides an O(n^3) implementation, which we study on traveling-salesman problems (TSP). We derive conditional repaired-success bounds and quantify how basin aggregation reduces the absolute-transfer budget required by these bounds. Noiseless simulations show that optimal repair basins contain selectively overweighted infeasible contributors. For an n=10 TSP instance, pushforward repair recovered the optimum using approximately 10^3 shots, compared with 10^6 shots in the original CE-QAOA workflow without repair. On a 127-qubit IBM processor, using encodings of up to 100 qubits, repaired candidates match reference tours on smaller benchmarks and improve them on larger instances. These results establish concentration of quantum probability on useful repair preimages as a design principle for constrained quantum optimization.
item.dc:creator: Chinonso Onah, Stuart Hadfield, Kristel Michielsen

item.title: Service-Area Robust NOMA for Pinching Antennas Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) enable near-field beam focusing using radiating points along a dielectric waveguide, but coherent spherical-wave superposition makes their channels sensitive to small user displacements. This sensitivity is critical for power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), where successive interference cancellation (SIC) requires the weak-user layer to remain decodable at the strong user. We develop spatially robust PASS-NOMA designs that optimize antenna placement and power splitting over bounded service areas (SAs), with a preset decoding order and explicit SIC-feasibility constraints. We propose a worst-case design for quasi-static users and an ergodic design for codewords spanning representative SA positions, and characterize their achievable rate regions. Numerical results show that, despite SIC requiring weak-user decoding in both SAs, NOMA outperforms orthogonal multiple access (OMA) with a shared placement under both robustness models except when the strong user is served at low rate. In the ergodic regime, this advantage can persist even against OMA with per-user antenna reconfiguration.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Wireless Communications Letters, Date of Publication: 30 October 2026
item.dc:creator: Zoran Hadzi-Velkov, Slavche Pejoski, Jia Guo, Marija Poposka, Arumugam Nallanathan

item.title: Low-PAPR Rank-2 DFT-s-OFDM Waveform for 6G Uplink
item.description: arXiv:2611.00862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rank-2 discrete Fourier transform-spread orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (DFT-s-OFDM) is attracting renewed interest for 6G uplink, offering not only spatial multiplexing gains but also an additional degree of freedom for peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction. We exploit this freedom by selectively exchanging constellation symbols between the two layers before DFT spreading, preserving the transmitted information while reshaping the resulting waveforms. Building on this idea, we propose Cyclic Layer Assignment with Shared-basis Synthesis (CLASS). CLASS employs carefully designed cyclic assignment patterns to generate diverse waveform candidates, while reusing a small number of waveform components to avoid synthesizing each candidate separately. We further establish the optimality of the cyclic design in maximizing waveform diversity under a minimum-basis constraint when equal group sizes are feasible. With only six inverse DFTs, CLASS explores 16 assignments and reduces the 99th-percentile worst-layer PAPR by 1.41 dB relative to fixed assignment, outperforming representative selected mapping (SLM) and partial transmit sequences (PTS) schemes under the same synthesis budget.
item.dc:creator: Yewen Cao, Fen Hou, Yulin Shao

item.title: The covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code in nine variables is 242
item.description: arXiv:2611.00890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the covering radius of the binary first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242. Equivalently, the maximum nonlinearity of a Boolean function in nine variables is 242. Our proof combines a one-point rigidity theorem with a spectral and computational exclusion of the two larger candidate nonlinearities. We first show that every nine-variable Boolean function of nonlinearity 243 admits a unique one-point modification that raises its nonlinearity to 244: the point to be changed is the vector sum of its support. This part uses exact Walsh-update identities, integer interpolation, rigidity of a quadratic residue, and a sharp Walsh l1 estimate for cubic Boolean functions. To exclude nonlinearity 244, we use Parseval's identity and congruences of integral Walsh coefficients to force an exceptionally restricted spectrum. An associated cubic residue phase must attain the extremal Walsh l1 bound 10240. We eliminate one equality spectrum by hyperplane slicing; the other forces the original Boolean function from the signs of the cubic phase and yields a double-complement-pairing identity for its cubic top part. The classification of alternating trilinear forms over F2, an exact filter of their representatives, and two exhaustive enumerations of 218 quadratic supplements then rule out every remaining candidate. Together with the known construction attaining nonlinearity 242, these arguments establish the asserted covering radius.
item.dc:creator: Yi Li

item.title: Latin cubes of order $4$ and $4320$-point quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00927v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Possibly the most enduring lower-bound record for kissing numbers in dimensions greater than $8$ (excluding $24$) is $$ \kappa_{16}\geq 4320. $$ This lower bound is attained by a shell of the famous Barnes--Wall lattice, which was discovered in 1959. Besides this configuration, at least one alternative $4320$-point kissing arrangement is currently known. Recently, it was noticed that all these configurations can be described in terms of the so-called quaternionic construction, a general type of construction that was instrumental in explaining the geometry of the $841$-point kissing arrangement in ${\mathbb R}^{12}$. We give a simple generalization of quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$ obtained from record configurations. They are parameterized by three Latin cubes of order $4$, six permutations of $3$-element set, and are all infinitesimally jammed. Computer-aided counting shows that there are $4\,072\,728\,621$ isometry classes in this family of $4320$-point kissing arrangements.
item.dc:creator: Rustem Takhanov

item.title: Bilinear Hulls for Support Splitting: Characterization, Optimization, and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.01337v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sendrier's Support Splitting Algorithm (SSA) is the standard solver for the Permutation Equivalence Problem (PEP); its cost is dominated by a term that grows exponentially in the hull dimension. We study, mathematically, how much this cost can be lowered by replacing the standard inner product, on which the hull is defined, with an alternative bilinear form. Two structural results give a complete answer: only a narrow two-parameter family of bilinear forms produces a hull on which SSA can still operate, namely those whose matrix in the standard basis is a linear combination of the identity and the all-ones matrix; and even within this family the hull dimension drops by at most one (with the reduction achieved on every self-dual code whose length is coprime to the field characteristic). Together, these results give a tight upper bound: since SSA on a code with hull dimension $h$ has cost dominated by $q^h$, replacing the standard hull with $\mathrm{Hull}_M$ lowers this dominant term from $q^h$ to at best $q^{h-1}$, so no bilinear-form generalization of the inner product can reduce the SSA cost by more than a factor of $q$, the field size. Going beyond this requires invariants outside the bilinear framework. As an application, we verify that PEP-based SPECK admits the factor-$q$ cost reduction, while LEP-based LESS and PKP-based PERK lie outside our framework. A SageMath implementation of the bilinear-hull preprocessing confirms feasibility at SPECK's recommended length $n = 252$.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Aikawa, Keita Ishizuka, Tomoki Moriya

item.title: Assessing Temporal Dispersion of Time-Varying Channel at 38 GHz for Different Reference Signals
item.description: arXiv:2611.01685v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates the influence of reference waveform selection on temporal dispersion estimation in a time-varying radio channel at 38 GHz. Three reference waveforms-numerically generated in MATLAB, measured through a conducted connection, and recorded in an anechoic chamber -are compared using the same wideband channel measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment. Their effects on the estimated power delay profiles (PDPs), mean delay, and root mean square (RMS) delay spread are evaluated.
