Despite noticeable differences in the time-domain and spectral characteristics of the reference waveforms, the resulting PDPs exhibit similar multipath structures, while the estimated temporal dispersion parameters show relatively small differences. The results indicate limited sensitivity to reference waveform selection under the investigated measurement conditions.
item.dc:creator: Jaros{\l}aw Wojtu\'n, Bartosz Czaja, Tomasz Grasza, Rafa{\l} Przesmycki, Jan M. Kelner, Cezary Zi\'o{\l}kowski, Radek Zavorka, Josef Vychodil, Tomas Mikulasek, Jiri Blumenstein, Ales Prokes, Aniruddha Chandra

item.title: Ray-Tracing-Parameter-Based Lightweight Hybrid Precoding via Cascade XGBoost for Wideband Massive MIMO-OFDM Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hybrid precoding reduces the radio-frequency (RF) hardware burden in wideband massive MIMO-OFDM systems, but conventional optimization and deep neural network (DNN)-based approaches can incur high online complexity. This paper proposes XGB-SVD, a lightweight hybrid precoding framework that maps compact ray-tracing path parameters directly to analog beamforming codeword indices using cascade eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). The cascade captures sequential beam-selection dependencies and transmit--receive propagation correlation, while the digital precoder and combiner are obtained from the reduced-dimensional equivalent channel using singular value decomposition (SVD). Evaluations over five DeepMIMO scenarios spanning sub-6-GHz and millimeter-wave bands show that XGB-SVD consistently outperforms the considered DNN baselines and approaches simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) in several environments. Cross-scenario results further indicate improved transfer from propagation-diverse training environments, while XGB-SVD provides lower online computational and training costs than the DNN baselines.
item.dc:creator: Po-Heng Chou, Wei-Chen Lin, Wan-Jen Huang, Walid Saad, Ronald Y. Chang

item.title: Green Learning-Based Signal-Level Detection of RIS Spoofing Attacks in Vehicular ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless infrastructure to jointly support communication and environmental sensing, but also introduces new physical-layer security threats. A malicious reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) can manipulate its time-varying reflection phases to generate spoofing echoes and distort the sensing results of a roadside unit (RSU). Existing trajectory-level detectors rely on reconstructed sensing parameters and vehicle trajectories, making their performance dependent on upstream estimation accuracy. In this paper, we propose a signal-level Green Learning (GL) framework that directly detects RIS spoofing from matched-filtered RSU echoes. The proposed method combines two-stage Subspace Approximation with Adjusted Bias (SAAB), Discriminant Feature Test (DFT), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for spatial-temporal representation learning, feature selection, and classification, respectively. Simulation results show 99.335\% detection accuracy for a 32-element malicious RIS at $-80$ dBm receiver noise power. GL remains competitive with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) baselines while requiring only 0.1119 million floating-point operations (FLOPs), and also generalizes to previously unseen RIS sizes.
item.dc:creator: Po-Heng Chou, Tingyu Shui, Pin-Qi Fu, Lien-Sheng Chang, Walid Saad, Li-Chun Wang

item.title: Federated Estimation of Loading Spaces in Tensor Factor Models under Differential Privacy
item.description: arXiv:2611.01903v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tensor factor models provide low-dimensional representations of tensor-valued observations while preserving their multiway structure. When these observations are held by different clients, privacy constraints may prevent them from being pooled for centralized analysis. We study estimation of common loading spaces in Tucker tensor factor models under federated differential privacy, allowing heterogeneous sample sizes, privacy budgets, and factor strengths. The proposed method combines private stability testing, Huber aggregation, and Gaussian perturbation at each client with weighted aggregation at the server. We establish non-asymptotic upper bounds governed by a scaled harmonic mean of the squared local error rates, and prove minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors under strong factors, fixed factor ranks, and fixed noise variance. We further develop a private calibration procedure that selects the local tuning parameters and aggregation weights without knowledge of the noise level or client-specific factor strengths. The resulting adaptive estimator preserves the privacy guarantee and attains the error rate obtained with oracle tuning. We illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators through simulation experiments and an application to a Meditation Traits EEG dataset.
item.dc:creator: Zetai Cen, Fan Wang, Haeran Cho

item.title: Improved lower bounds for the kissing number in dimensions 49 to 61
item.description: arXiv:2611.01906v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give explicit kissing configurations in R^d for every d = 49, ..., 61. The lower bound is improved over the best previously published value in all thirteen dimensions, by margins from 232 to 159,220 points and by 506,461 points in total. The configurations are obtained from the antipodal block lift of Yang et al. applied to the 52,416,000-point minimal shell of the extremal even unimodular lattice P_48p, using a class of 7,193 minimal lines and, in each dimension, a kissing configuration of R^k (k <= 15) with the largest available number of antipodal pairs. Two ingredients are new. The published class of 7,077 lines is grown to 7,193 by local search in three stages, as a sequence of exchanges between candidate lines and class lines; and the point count, which equals 52,416,000 + 2S + 2t with t the number of antipodal pairs and S the size of the union of t isometric images of the class, is maximised as a maximum-coverage problem by greedy search with iterated local search over pools of 4,000 automorphic images, reaching 92-100% of the trivial bound 7,193t. All results are verified in exact integer arithmetic, and the certificates are distributed with the code. Code and data: https://github.com/dimkadimon/KissingNumbers
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Kamenetsky

item.title: A Beam-Switched Sparse Circular Array for Passive Wi-Fi Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.02378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wi-Fi sensing applications require unambiguous angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation over the full azimuth plane. Uniform circular arrays (UCAs) are shown to remove this ambiguity, but deploying the four RF chains typically available on commercial Wi-Fi chipsets into a sparse layout suffers from spatial undersampling. Such undersampling produces strong grating lobes. To overcome this hardware bottleneck, we first establish a generalized array manifold incorporating element radiation patterns, revealing the suitability and degradation mechanisms of directional UCAs. Then we propose an angularly staggered beam-switched UCA architecture that leverages the spatial complementarity. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed scheme effectively mitigates grating-lobe ambiguities without increasing the number of RF chains, significantly reducing AoA estimation outliers and improving omnidirectional tracking performance.
item.dc:creator: Yang Chen, Riccardo Bersan, Daniele Piazza, Stefano Savazzi, Michele D'Amico

item.title: Nearest Is Not Safest: Fluid-Antenna Port Selection for Over-the-Air Backpropagation in Urban Multipath
item.description: arXiv:2611.02384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Over-the-air backpropagation returns a loss gradient through the reciprocal channel, which requires the return port to see the channel of the forward port. If the terminal moves in between, a fluid antenna system can return through the port nearest to the forward position. In ray-traced Chicago streets, with a pedestrian displacement of about half a wavelength and a street-level base station, this rule reverses 20 percent of the gradients at a port spacing of 0.7 wavelengths and 49 percent at 0.9 wavelengths, while one of the four nearest ports stays aligned in all but 2 and 9 percent. We derive a certificate for the sign of the mean correlation from the second moment of a planar angular spectrum. It reduces to a linear program with three variables and infinitely many constraints, is tight, and holds over a region of second moments. In a static Gaussian model, observations collected along a line cannot tell an angular spectrum from its mirror image, so the sign of the cross moment must come from other information. At unsurveyed positions of the same city, a knowledge map that transports surveyed paths through virtual sources and fits them to the causal channel history lowers the reversal rate at 0.9 wavelengths from 49 to 27 percent. Its gain over the nearest port survived every tested error, while its gain over a geometry rule stayed significant at the tested single-error levels of 5 degrees of phase drift per step and 2 mm of position error but not at the next tested levels. Without any survey, across five cities and ten base stations, the nearest port reverses 37 percent of the returns at 0.9 wavelengths and a rule based on the direction and elevation of the base station 20.5 percent. The multilayer perceptrons we tested did not beat these physical rules by the margin fixed in advance in the primary settings.
item.dc:creator: Xianzhong Li, Yuzhi Yang, Tianhao Guo

item.title: Which Chains to Calibrate for Physical Backpropagation: Per-User Factors Versus Base-Station Chains
item.description: arXiv:2611.02390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In physical backpropagation, users return loss derivatives over the time-division duplex uplink, giving the base station the downlink gradient without channel reconstruction. Reciprocity calibration conventionally prioritizes base-station chains, as column-normalized zero-forcing reduces a per-user factor to a stream rotation. This priority can reverse. With ideal base-station chains and no noise, per-user amplitude errors make the returned field a weighted sum-rate gradient. With zero-forcing full service at both optima, the loss is independent of array size. Otherwise the selection penalty, serving the wrong users, carries 86 to 94 percent of the amplitude-induced loss in five of six configurations. Per-user phase errors mainly slow the iteration. Base-station chain errors scale the returned field per antenna, and at 3 dB and 25 degrees they cost one user 1.3 dB of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) that no array size removes. With 80 users, such errors on both sides, and mismatched pilots, oracle per-user and base-station calibration leave 6.2 and 12.3 percent loss at 256 antennas on clustered channels. This ordering holds at 30 dB SNR and reverses for 1 dB, 10 degree user errors. A capped one-echo estimator comes within 2.4 percentage points of oracle per-user calibration but underperforms no calibration at 10 dB SNR.
item.dc:creator: Xianzhong Li, Yuzhi Yang, Tianhao Guo

item.title: Finite attainment and efficient computation of regularized quantum channel relative entropy
item.description: arXiv:2611.02425v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum channel relative entropy can be nonadditive, making its regularization essential for asymptotic analysis. We study when the regularized value is attained at finite blocklength and how efficiently it can be approximated. For the first question, we establish a sharp dichotomy: the regularized value is either attained already at the single-copy level, implying additivity at every blocklength, or is never attained at any finite blocklength. Notably, a simple two-copy additivity test distinguishes between these alternatives for qubit channels and for channel pairs in arbitrary dimensions admitting an interior optimizer. We further show that both the interiority condition and finite nonattainment are generic, holding for almost every channel pair. For the second question, we establish explicit convergence rates for approximating the regularized channel relative entropy. For fixed channel dimensions, $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ channel copies suffice to approximate the regularized value to additive accuracy $\varepsilon$. Alternatively, a semidefinite hierarchy achieves the same accuracy at level $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-2})$, yielding a certified polynomial-time approximation. Together, these results reveal the intriguing structure and generic behavior of regularized channel relative entropy, sharpening our understanding of both its analytical and computational aspects.
item.dc:creator: Yiwei Xu, Kun Fang

item.title: Explicit permutations of $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ with uniformly bounded differential uniformity
item.description: arXiv:2611.02572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetric primitives over Galois rings need nonlinear components whose differentials with respect to ring addition are controlled. Let $R=\mathrm{GR}(4,m)$ and $q=2^m$, so that $(R,+)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ has order $N=q^2$. For every $m\ge1$ we construct an explicit permutation $G_c$ of $R$ all of whose differentials with a nonzero input difference have probability at most $36/N$, whereas every permutation polynomial of $R$ has such a differential of probability at least $2/\sqrt{N}$ (Ronjom--Sandrib). The bound holds for the fixed permutation itself, not on average over keys. Equivalently, $\Delta(G_c)\le36$ against $\Delta\ge2\sqrt{N}$ for permutation polynomials; since every permutation has $\Delta\ge2$, the least differential uniformity of a permutation of $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ lies between $2$ and $36$ for every $m$. In Teichmuller digits $(a,b)\in\mathbb{F}_q^2$ and for $c\in\mathbb{F}_q$ of absolute trace $1$, $G_c(a,b)=(L,(L^2+L+c)a)$ with $L=(a^2+a+c)b$. The map is $F_c\circ J\circ F_c$, where $F_c(a,b)=(a,(a^2+a+c)b)$ is induced by a polynomial over $R$ and $J$ exchanges the digits: a single digit exchange between two polynomial layers yields a bound independent of $m$. The proof reduces the difference equations, in each of three types of directions, to one-variable polynomials whose degrees do not depend on $m$. For general maps $F\circ J\circ F$ with $F(a,b)=(p(a),h(a)+d(a)b)$, where $p,d,h$ have degrees bounded independently of $m$, $p'\ne0$ and $d$ has no zeros, a Jacobian identity in characteristic $2$ bounds the differentials with nonzero low input and output differences independently of $m$; the remaining directions need a separate argument, which we give for an explicit family ($\Delta\le440$, resp. $510$, for odd $m$).
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Fukui

item.title: Equivalent Graphical Conditions for Angle Rigidity and Angle-Based Network Localization
item.description: arXiv:2611.02764v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Angle rigidity theory provides a theoretical basis for characterizing the geometric shape of graphs embedded in the plane under angle constraints, and establishing global convergence of angle-based network localization algorithms. The related references, however, are largely restricted to graphs generated by triangulation or bilateration ordering, which are sufficient but not necessary for angle rigidity. This paper addresses this challenge by focusing on establishing the equivalence between angle constraints and bearing constraints. The conditions for cycle compatible frameworks (with possibly non-generic configurations) to be angle fixable are provided. Moreover, it is shown for the first time that Laman graphs equivalently characterize minimally globally angle rigid graphs, implying that a Laman graph is the simplest graph that allows a generic embedding in the plane to be uniquely determined by subtended angles. As an application, a distributed algorithm for angle-based sensor network localization is proposed, which guarantees global convergence under a much milder network topology condition than those in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Jinpeng Huang, Gangshan Jing, Kai Zhao, Yongduan Song

item.title: Resilient Cell-Free MIMO ISAC Under Uncertainties: An Impairment-Aware Graph Neural Network Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.03054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Beamforming designs for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in cell-free multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems face the challenge to stay reliable under uncertainties from both channel state information (CSI) as well as clutter. To this end, this paper proposes an impairment-aware heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) framework for beamforming that obtains the CSI error level and the clutter covariance as edge features, which enables a single trained model to adapt to both impairments. In particular, the GNN is trained on a low quantile of the minimum user rate with a clutter-aware signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio, balanced by a normalized Tchebycheff scalarization. Simulation results show that the proposed GNN framework outperforms the considered baselines in sensing-only and communication-only settings. Depending on the operating point, a single GNN model attains approximately 97\% of each baseline's rate while serving both functionalities at once. The model further generalizes to unseen CSI error levels and clutter counts and renders the ISAC system resilient.
item.dc:creator: Oways Alsoloh, Robert-Jeron Reifert, Aymen Khaleel, Stefan Roth, Aydin Sezgin

item.title: Belief Propagation-Informed Tesseract Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In quantum error correction, the decoder must estimate the errors from the measurement data accurately and fast enough to avoid a backlog. Search-based decoders such as Tesseract achieve high accuracy by finding a minimum-weight set of error events with an A* search, but their search effort grows rapidly with the physical error rate and the code size. To reduce this search effort while maintaining a logical error rate close to that of Tesseract, we propose a belief propagation (BP)-guided modification of the Tesseract decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Damped sum-product BP is applied to the triggered detectors before the Tesseract search. If the detectors triggered by the BP hard decision match the triggered detectors, this hard decision is accepted directly, and the Tesseract search is skipped. Otherwise, the BP marginal probability estimates, weighted by a trust coefficient, modify the search priority, while the path cost keeps the channel-prior weights so that the decoding objective is unchanged. The framework also supports BP-based initialization, in which selected BP decisions form the starting point of a residual search whose signed-cost objective allows incorrect initial decisions to be removed. A node-exploration limit bounds this residual search; if the limit is reached, the decoder falls back to the BP-guided search on the original triggered detector set. The method is evaluated on the [[72,12,6]], [[90,8,10]], and [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle codes under circuit-level noise. With BP-based initialization and a global trust coefficient, the number of Tesseract search nodes expanded is reduced by up to more than two orders of magnitude at low physical error rates, while the logical error rate remains close to that of Tesseract.
item.dc:creator: Sana Javed, Francisco Garcia-Herrero, Bane Vasi\'c, Mark F. Flanagan

item.title: Finite-Memory Control of POMDPs: Fundamental Limits and Efficient Design
item.description: arXiv:2611.03414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optimal control of partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs), in general, requires a complete history. The belief state, a distribution over hidden states, summarizes this history and provides the classical sufficient statistic to control POMDPs. However, the continuous nature of the belief space generally prevents a finite-memory controller from maintaining it exactly. This raises the question we address in this work: what must the available finite memory preserve to achieve near-optimal control performance? We study this question through an information-theoretic converse that gives a fundamental lower bound on the loss of any finite-memory controller. The analysis introduces the concept of a decision witness that characterizes belief states whose confusion would lead to unavoidable loss. Motivated by this bound, we propose RECAP, a constructive quantization method for designing representative memory states. We prove an upper bound on the optimality gap of any RECAP codebook and use the components of this bound together with the converse analysis to define the codebook objective. Experiments on 11 POMDP benchmarks demonstrate that RECAP improves over finite-memory representation baselines under the same memory budget.
item.dc:creator: Emrecan Kutay, Atilla Eryilmaz, Ness Shroff

item.title: On the Failure Probability of Quantum Leftover Hashing with Bad Seeds
item.description: arXiv:2611.03484v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study hashing against quantum adversaries, as used in cryptographic applications, and provide bounds on the probability of failure in practical settings where seeds might be reused and might be non-ideal. Randomness extraction and privacy amplification are key components of quantum cryptographic protocols, such as quantum randomness generation or key distribution, that allow the compression of partially secure raw data into shorter output with high security. To ensure the security of any cryptographic construction that integrates them, it is desirable to establish composable security. This can be done by using methods based on universal hashing and leveraging the general leftover hash lemma, which allows extraction of near-uniform random numbers from an imperfect entropy source by sampling from an almost two-universal family of hash functions using a seed. This approach is taken in many practical implementations, commonly using Toeplitz hashing. The lemma provides an upper bound $\varepsilon$ on the distance of the output to uniform randomness, which holds on average over the choice of seeds. It makes no claim that any particular seed yields near-uniform random numbers. This poses a problem for practical applications where a seed is sampled once and reused for many rounds (blockwise hashing). Here, we study the subset of \textit{bad} seeds yielding far-from-uniform outputs. We show that randomness extraction against quantum side information is guaranteed to produce $\delta$-close-to-uniform random numbers except with failure probability $\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{\delta}\right)^2$. This result is generalised to blockwise hashing providing a guarantee of the security of $k$ rounds except with failure probability $\big(\frac{(2k-1)\varepsilon}{\delta}\big)^2$. Moreover, we extend the general leftover hash lemma to blockwise hashing and relax the assumption of almost two-universality.
item.dc:creator: Asker Friis Bach, Isabel Moreno Babuglia, Jonatan Bohr Brask

item.title: Should We Combine Our Data? Algorithms and Limits for Privately Assessing Data Sharing
item.description: arXiv:2611.03599v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study when two parties should pool their data to train a machine learning model. Two agents, Alice and Bob, each hold a sensitive labeled dataset and want to train a classifier from a given hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}$. Even when each party's dataset can be perfectly classified on its own, the two parties may follow conflicting labeling standards or have selection biases that affect their features and label sets, such that no single classifier in $\mathcal{H}$ fits their combined data. Before committing to data sharing, Alice and Bob therefore want to test whether a single classifier in $\mathcal{H}$ can jointly fit both datasets---without revealing their individual data points to one another. We formalize this problem from a learning-theoretic viewpoint via $\operatorname{opt}_\mathcal{H}$, the minimum \emph{number of mistakes} made by any hypothesis in $\mathcal{H}$ on their pooled data. Through interactive communication, the agents must distinguish $\operatorname{opt}_\mathcal{H}=0$ (compatible datasets) from $\operatorname{opt}_\mathcal{H}\geq t$ (conflicting datasets) under pure $\varepsilon$-two-party differential privacy. A trusted curator could do this with $t=O(1/\varepsilon)$, and we ask how small $t$ can be without one. For thresholds on the real line over a domain of size $m$, we show that the optimal $t$ is $\tilde{\Theta}(\log\log m/\varepsilon)$, exponentially smaller than the $\Theta(\log m/\varepsilon)$ samples needed to privately learn thresholds, even with a curator. For halfspaces in $\mathbb{R}^d$, the dependence on $m$ jumps to $\log(m)$: we give a protocol with $t=\tilde{O}(d^3\log m/\varepsilon)$ and show that some domains require $t=\Omega(d\log(m/d)/\varepsilon)$.
item.dc:creator: Mahdi Haghifam, Kumar Kshitij Patel, Avrim Blum, Giulia Fanti, Juba Ziani

item.title: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.03639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum channel tomography (also known as quantum process tomography) is a fundamental task in quantum information and quantum computing, aiming to learn the full description of an unknown quantum channel from black-box queries. For channels with input dimension $d_1$, output dimension $d_2$, and Kraus rank at most $r$, [CGO+26] identifies the dilation rate $\tau=rd_2/d_1\geq 1$ as a key parameter governing a Heisenberg-to-classical transition in query complexity. While the optimal bounds in the boundary regime ($\tau=1$) and the away-from-boundary regime ($\tau\geq 1+\Omega(1)$) are now known, the precise behavior in the near-boundary regime ($1<\tau<1+o(1)$) has remained unresolved. In this paper, we close this gap, thereby fully settling the query complexity of quantum channel tomography. Specifically, we show that the query complexity is - $\Omega(rd_1d_2/\varepsilon^2)$ for diamond norm error $\varepsilon$, matching the upper bound by [MB26, CGO+26], - $\Theta(d_1^2/\varepsilon+\min\{(\tau-1)d_1^2,(\tau-1)^2d_1^2d_2^2\}/\varepsilon^2)$ for Choi trace norm error $\varepsilon$. Our results reveal two qualitatively different forms of the Heisenberg-to-classical transition. For diamond norm tomography, the Heisenberg scaling disappears suddenly as soon as $\tau$ leaves the boundary regime. In contrast, Choi trace norm tomography exhibits a gradual transition from Heisenberg to classical scaling as $\tau$ moves from the boundary regime to the away-from-boundary regime.
item.dc:creator: Kean Chen, Aadil Oufkir

item.title: Over-fitting Control in Deep Nonlinear Matrix Completion via Gradual Nonsmooth Regularization
item.description: arXiv:2403.10232v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Conventional matrix completion methods exploit the underlying low-rank structure of a target matrix to recover its missing entries, but may be inadequate for capturing complex nonlinear dependencies. Deep neural networks have therefore been increasingly adopted for nonlinear matrix completion (NLMC). However, their high representational capacity, particularly in deep fully connected neural networks (FCNNs), can lead to over-fitting when training is restricted to incomplete observations. In this paper, we propose a Deep Neural Network with Nonsmooth Regularization (DNN-NSR) framework to address this issue by incorporating two complementary structural priors: sparsity of intermediate representations and low-rankness of layer-wise weight matrices. Specifically, the $\ell_1$-norm of hidden representations promotes sparse latent features, while the nuclear norm of weight matrices encourages low-rank layer-wise transformations. To optimize the resulting nonsmooth and nonconvex objective, we develop an extrapolated proximal gradient algorithm that employs soft-thresholding and singular-value thresholding to handle the two regularization terms, respectively. We further introduce a gradual regularization strategy that progressively increases the influence of these structural penalties during training. Under suitable assumptions, we establish convergence properties of the proposed algorithm toward a critical point of the training objective. The effectiveness of DNN-NSR is evaluated through extensive experiments on synthetic matrix recovery, single-image inpainting, and recommender systems using the MovieLens 100K and MovieLens 1M datasets. Comparisons with representative linear and nonlinear matrix completion methods demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to improve recovery performance by jointly exploiting sparse latent representations and low-rank network transformations.
item.dc:creator: Sajad Faramarzi, Farzan Haddadi, Sajjad Amini, Masoud Ahookhosh, Symeon Chatzinotas

item.title: Demystifying 5G Polar and LDPC Codes: A Comprehensive Review and Foundations
item.description: arXiv:2502.11053v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding how 5G networks correct errors is no trivial matter. At the heart of the process lie two sophisticated families of codes: LDPC and polar codes. This paper opens the black box, not only by explaining how these codes are designed, but also by showing how they are encoded and decoded in practice. To describe the research covered in this review, we present a detailed survey of the literature supplemented with insights that are often buried deep within technical standards. These foundations are not just historical footnotes: they remain relevant to research on error correction for future wireless systems. In bringing clarity to these building blocks, we aim to help engineers and researchers navigate what is both a complex and increasingly vital part of wireless communication.
item.dc:creator: Mody Sy

item.title: Transversal gates for quantum CSS codes
item.description: arXiv:2601.21514v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we focus on the problem of computing the set of diagonal transversal gates fixing a CSS code. We determine the logical actions of these gates and characterize the subgroups that induce tensor products of single-qubit logical gates and logical identities. We describe these groups through explicit linear equations given by componentwise products of basis vectors of the underlying classical codes, which is the key difference from previous approaches. We compute the complete set of diagonal transversal gates fixing the code, and of transversal logical gates, for any CSS code arising from monomial codes, a family that includes decreasing monomial codes and polar codes. As a consequence, we recover and extend some results in the literature on CSS-T codes, triorthogonal codes, and divisible codes. We also extend these results to diagonal gates acting transversally on several code blocks and use them to characterize addressable gates.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Camps-Moreno, Hiram H. L\'opez, Gretchen L. Matthews, Narayanan Rengaswamy, Rodrigo San-Jos\'e

item.title: The mathematical landscape of partial information decomposition: A comprehensive review of properties and measures
item.description: arXiv:2603.06678v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partial Information Decomposition (PID) has become one of the most prominent information-theoretic frameworks for describing the structure and quality of information in complex systems. Despite its widespread utility, there exists no unique solution constraining precisely how a PID should be constructed, leading to a multiverse of different formalisms with different mathematical commitments. In this work, we provide a comprehensive overview of the mathematical landscape of PID. By integrating existing PID measures into a common language, we systematically examine all major approaches to the PID framework that have emerged so far, determining for each measure whether or not each known property holds. In addition, we derive a web of all known theorems mapping the relationships and incompatibilities between these properties, before also revealing some novel interdependency results. In doing so, we chart a brief history of the framework, promote a unified perspective for its discussions, and offer a path towards both theoretical refinement and informed empirical applications for the future of this powerful method.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Liardi, Keenan J. A. Down, George Blackburne, Matteo Neri, Pedro A. M. Mediano

item.title: Minimizing the Age of Incorrect Information of Discrete-Time Markov Sources With Hybrid ARQ
item.description: arXiv:2603.28369v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work introduces a framework for analyzing the Age of Incorrect Information (AoII) in a real-time monitoring system with a generic discrete-time Markov source. We study a noisy communication system employing a hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) protocol, subject to a transmission rate constraint. The optimization problem is formulated as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP), and it is shown that there exists an optimal policy that is a randomized mixture of two stationary policies. To overcome the intractability of computing the optimal stationary policies, we develop a multiple-threshold policy class where thresholds depend on the source, the receiver, and the packet count. By establishing a Markov renewal structure induced by threshold policies, we derive closed-form expressions for the long-term average AoII and transmission rate. The proposed policy is constructed via a relative value iteration algorithm that leverages the threshold structure to skip computations, combined with a bisection search to satisfy the rate constraint. To accommodate scenarios requiring lower computational complexity, we adapt the same technique to produce a simpler single-threshold policy that trades optimality for efficiency. Numerical experiments exhibit that both thresholdbased policies outperform periodic scheduling, with the multiplethreshold approach matching the performance of the globally optimal policy.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Bountrogiannis, Anthony Ephremides, Panagiotis Tsakalides, George Tzagkarakis

item.title: Capacity-Aware Multi-UE Handover Optimization for LEO Satellite Networks Using Dueling DDQN
item.description: arXiv:2605.02416v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Frequent handovers and finite satellite capacity make multi-user mobility management challenging in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks. This paper develops a capacity-aware multi-user handover framework based on a double deep Q-network (DDQN) with a dueling architecture. Both training and evaluation employ sequential user equipment (UE) processing with shared satellite occupancy, while action masking excludes invisible or capacity-infeasible satellites. The state incorporates satellite visibility, achievable link quality, remaining capacity, previous association, short-term visibility, and time information. A fixed multi-criteria reward balances throughput, blocking, handover cost, connection persistence, and short-term visibility, while expert trajectories are used only for replay-buffer initialization. Simulations under different UE densities and satellite capacities show that the proposed framework maintains high average throughput per UE and low blocking rates with moderate handover frequency. Ablation results show that removing the remaining-capacity vector has only a limited effect on performance when sequential occupancy tracking and feasible-action masking are retained.
item.dc:creator: Po-Heng Chou, Chiapin Wang, Chung-Chi Huang, Kuan-Hao Chen, Chien-Yu Chen

item.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions
item.description: arXiv:2606.11987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lifted product codes are an important family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, as they were the first QLDPC code family shown to be asymptotically good. Understanding the structure of their parity-check matrices $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$, as well as the associated Tanner graphs, is essential for analyzing their decoding behavior and error-floor performance. In this work, we show that the Tanner graphs of $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$ are indeed isomorphic, and investigate their graph-theoretical structure. We establish conditions ensuring the connectivity of these graphs and provide bounds on their minimal absorbing sets, providing new insight into the combinatorial structures influencing decoding performance.
item.dc:creator: Ragnar Freij-Hollanti, Kirsten D. Morris, Patricija \v{S}apokait\.e

item.title: Limits of Finite-Sample Dependence Measures under Data Processing Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2606.14225v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study dependence measures between two discrete random variables. The measures vanish at independence and satisfy the data processing inequality (DPI): stochastic post-processing of one variable cannot increase dependence. We ask which such measures admit an exactly unbiased estimator from a fixed finite number of i.i.d. samples, a property equivalent to being polynomial in the joint probabilities. We distinguish fixed-alphabet DPI, which preserves the alphabet size of the variable being processed, from dimension-changing DPI. Under one-sided fixed-alphabet DPI, every measure with a continuously differentiable extension to a neighborhood of the closed probability simplex vanishes whenever one processed state has zero probability. If the processed alphabet is larger than the other alphabet, the measure is identically zero. If it has $n$ states and the other alphabet has at least $n$, every nonzero polynomial measure has degree at least $2n$ and requires at least $2n$ samples for unbiased estimation. Both bounds are attained by the Gram determinant. Under one-sided dimension-changing DPI, every family with the same boundary regularity is identically zero. These results yield sharp task bounds for multi-task peer prediction. For two agents with $n$ signals each, $2n$ tasks are necessary and sufficient for nontrivial expected payments that vanish for independent reports and cannot increase under memoryless stochastic garbling. Under these requirements, unequal signal-space sizes force the larger-alphabet agent's expected payment to vanish identically for any finite number of tasks.
item.dc:creator: Yuqing Kong

item.title: Discrepancy for Random Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2606.24471v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that random linear codes (RLCs) possess nearly optimal discrepancy-type properties in a broad range of settings. Our main results are two general discrepancy theorems: one controls all translates of a fixed test, and the other controls large families of Fourier-pseudorandom tests. Two motivating examples follow: First, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for list-decoding from errors above capacity. More precisely, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1 - \frac{1}{n}\log_q|B_\rho| + \varepsilon$, where $|B_\rho|$ is the volume of a radius-$\rho$ Hamming ball in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, satisfies $|C \cap B| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot |B|}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all radius-$\rho$ Hamming balls $B$ with high probability. This significantly strengthens the best prior results, which follow from work by Blinovsky (1987, 1990) and Levitin (1988) on the covering properties of RLCs. Second, over prime fields, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for zero-error list-recovery, and list-recovery from erasures, above capacity. More precisely, for a prime $q>2$ and input list size $2\leq \ell\leq q-1$, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1-\log_q \ell+\varepsilon$ will satisfy $|C \cap S| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot \ell^n}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all combinatorial rectangles $S=S_1\times S_2\times\cdots\times S_n$, where $|S_i|=\ell$ for all $i$, with high probability. An analogous result also holds when we can bound $|S_i|$ only for some of the $i$'s. We use this to show the abundance of locally leakage-resilient $n$-party linear ramp secret sharing schemes with any linear reconstruction threshold and sublinear threshold gap $O(n/\log n)$ over fields of polynomial size $q=\Theta(n^\gamma)$ for a constant $\gamma\in(0,1/5)$. Prior work was stuck at reconstruction thresholds above $n/2$ for both threshold and ramp schemes.
item.dc:creator: Dean Doron, Tal Leonov, Jonathan Mosheiff, Henrique Navas, Nicolas Resch, Jo\~ao Ribeiro

item.title: Antenna Orientation Optimization for Rotatable Antenna-Enabled ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2606.31466v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-fixed flexible antenna architectures, such as fluid antenna system (FAS), movable antenna (MA), and pinching antenna, have garnered significant interest in recent years. In this paper, we deploy a rotatable antenna (RA) array at the base station (BS) to improve the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) performance by exploiting the additional spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) introduced by antenna rotation. To enhance the sensing performance over an extended region containing a potential target while meeting the communication requirements of multiple users, we aim to maximize the minimum echo signal power within the sensing region, subject to required minimum communication rates of the users. For the special case of a single user and a point target, we develop a tractable approximation of the original problem, leading to independent per-RA subproblems. We characterize the geometric structure of these subproblems and derive closed-form solutions. Under the far-field approximation, the per-RA subproblems become approximately identical, allowing a common pointing vector to be adopted for all RAs. For the general multi-user and regional sensing case, we propose an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm that alternately optimizes the transmit beamforming for communication, the covariance matrix of the probing signal, and the pointing vectors of the RAs in an iterative manner. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RA-enabled ISAC system significantly outperforms various benchmark schemes with restricted antenna-orientation flexibility, while the evaluation of the Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB) further verifies its benefits for target-position estimation accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Qingjie Wu, Beixiong Zheng, Guangchi Zhang, Robert Schober

item.title: Three classes of few-weight self-orthogonal projective codes and their applications for LCD codes
item.description: arXiv:2607.07181v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Since self-orthogonal codes, few-weight codes and linear complementary dual codes(LCD codes, for short) have nice applications in coding theory and cryptography, they have received continuous attention. In 2024, by introducing the notion of the augment code, Heng et al.[16] constructed several classes of few-weight self-orthogonal codes basing on defining sets, which are introduced by Ding et al.[7] in 2007. In this manuscript, for two classes of defining sets, we consider the corresponding augmented codes, construct three classes of four-weight self-orthogonal projective codes and determine the parameters of their dual codes. And then, we construct three classes of LCD codes. In particular, we prove that there exists a class of these LCD codes whose dual codes are almost optimal LCD codes according to the sphere packing bound.
item.dc:creator: Yue Huang, Zhonghao Liang, Chenlu Jia, Yongkang Wan, Qunying Liao

item.title: Partial Path Interception in Derivation DAGs: Structural Complexity, Parameterized Algorithms, and Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2608.11782v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partial path interception (PPI) asks for a minimum-cost vertex set whose removal from a directed acyclic graph leaves at most a prescribed number of designated terminals able to reach a protected sink. We study how costs, depth, and fan-out affect its complexity. Unit-cost PPI is NP-complete at depth two with exactly two paths per terminal. Unique-path and individual-coverage instances admit polynomial-time algorithms, and bounded treewidth yields fixed-parameter tractability. Parameterized by the terminal threshold, weighted PPI is in XP and W-one-hard already at depth two, with no subexponential-time algorithm in that threshold under ETH. At depth two, undeletable terminals with bounded fan-out admit an FPT algorithm parameterized by the terminal threshold plus the fan-out bound. For unit costs, a dual-gammoid rank identity characterizes the optimum. Unit-cost depth-two instances with intermediate in-degree at most two are solvable in polynomial time for every terminal threshold, whereas depth-three instances are W-one-hard even with terminal out-degree one. On general directed acyclic graphs, minimum cuts and submodular optimization give a randomized approximation whose factor is the smaller of the coverage demand and roughly the square root of the number of initially exposed terminals, up to logarithmic factors. Reductions from smallest specified-edge subgraph, densest subgraph, and minimum union transfer conditional approximation lower bounds. PPI also gives an exact formulation of proof-valid caching under conjunctive derivation semantics: under independent premise erasures, the recovery probability equals one minus the erasure rate raised to the number of exposed premises. We extend this formulation to shared workloads, derive a sorting-based optimum under exact module routing, and give an AND-OR reliability envelope and a separate coded payload-recovery benchmark.
item.dc:creator: Jianfeng Xu

item.title: Optimal Condition Numbers in Low-Rank Positive Semidefinite Matrix Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2608.22418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we focus on the stability of positive semidefinite matrix sensing maps $\Phi_{\mathcal{A}}=(\langle A_i,X\rangle)_{i=1}^m$ where $A_i\succeq 0$, $X\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r$. We introduce the bi-Lipschitz constants of $\Phi_{\mathcal{A}}$ and define the global condition numbers as the ratio of upper and lower Lipschitz constants. We give deterministic universal lower bounds for these condition numbers that depend only on the rank $r$ and on the underlying field. We then show that rank-one Gaussian measurements asymptotically attain these bounds, except for the operator-norm condition number over $\mathbb R$ when $r=1$. For this exceptional case, we establish a sharper universal lower bound and prove its asymptotic sharpness. As an application, we derive stability guarantees for an $\ell_1$-residual PhaseLift-type estimator at the optimal sampling scale. These results identify the intrinsic limits of conditioning in positive semidefinite matrix sensing and connect these limits to stable low-rank recovery.
item.dc:creator: Mingxuan Sun, Zhiqiang Xu

item.title: Proximity Gaps for Gabidulin Codes and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2609.09838v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Proximity gaps are central to the soundness of interactive oracle proofs of proximity (IOPPs) and polynomial commitment schemes (PCSs). An $[n,k,d]$ linear code $C\subseteq\mathbb F^n$ has a $\delta$-proximity gap with error $\epsilon$ if, for every $u_0,u_1\in\mathbb F^n$, either all points on $\ell_{u_0,u_1}=\{u_0+\alpha u_1:\alpha\in\mathbb F\}$ are $\delta$-close to $C$, or at most an $\epsilon$ fraction are. Although proximity gaps for Hamming-metric codes are well understood, their rank-metric counterparts remain largely unexplored despite their applications in coding theory and cryptography. In this work, we study proximity gaps for linear rank-metric codes and their cryptographic applications. First, we show that every $[n,k,d]$ linear rank-metric code $C$ over $\mathbb F_{q^m}$ admits a proximity gap for every $\delta\le(d-1)/(3n)$, with error at most $q^{e+1}/q^m$, where $e=\lfloor\delta n\rfloor$. For Gabidulin codes, we improve the gap to $(d-1)/(2n)$ with error $10q^{n-1}/q^m$. These two proximity gaps match those for general linear Hamming-metric codes and Reed--Solomon (RS) codes, respectively. We prove the $(d-1)/(2n)$ bound is tight by constructing an infinite family of constant-rate Gabidulin codes and affine lines $\ell_{u_0,u_1}$ on which a $1-o(1)$ fraction of points are $d/(2n)$-close to the code, while $u_1$ is at least $3d/(4n)$-far from it. At $\delta=(d-1)/(2n)$, a further counterexample gives a lower bound of order $q^{n-1}/q^m$ on $\varepsilon$, matching our upper bound up to a constant factor. As applications, we construct an IOPP for interleaved Gabidulin codes by adapting the Ligero IOPP for interleaved RS codes. We then adapt the Ligero-based PCS for ordinary polynomials to obtain a $q$-linearized polynomial commitment scheme. To our knowledge, this is the first PCS framework based on rank-metric error-correcting codes.
item.dc:creator: Songsong Li, Chaoping Xing, Chen Yuan, Ruiqi Zhu

item.title: Exponentially Larger Deletion-Correcting Codes and Constant-List-Decodable Insertion-Deletion Codes
item.description: arXiv:2609.21395v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish improved asymptotic rate bounds for adversarial insertion--deletion codes. For binary unique-deletion correction in the linear-deletion regime, we strictly improve Levenshtein's classical lower-bound expression. At deletion fraction $\delta=0.1$, our achievable rate increases from $0.162009$ to $0.194890$, a relative gain of approximately $20.30\%$. For list decoding with any prescribed finite list size $L$, we obtain new achievable-rate bounds for binary deletion and insertion codes. Our approach combines the Lov\'asz local lemma with refined counting of common subsequences and supersequences, using generating functions and run-restricted sampling. We also establish a combinatorial reduction that trades $L$ units of insertion budget for one unit of deletion budget without changing the code or increasing the list size. It transfers insertion lower bounds at $\gamma+L\delta$ and deletion upper bounds at $\delta+\gamma/L$ to mixed errors. We also derive a run-counting Levenshtein-type list-decoding upper bound and a higher-order Elias-type upper bound. The latter recovers Yasunaga's asymptotic unique-decoding bound at $L=1$ and strictly improves the Haeupler--Shahrasbi--Sudan insertion upper bound for every fixed $L$ and $0<\gamma<q-1$. Numerical comparisons quantify the gains and the remaining gaps.
item.dc:creator: Han Mao Kiah, Hengjia Wei, Ruixiao Zeng

item.title: Dynamic Coded Distributed Computing with Joint File Placement and Reduce Function Reassignment
item.description: arXiv:2609.39373v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coded distributed computing (CDC) mitigates the Shuffle communication bottleneck through coded multicast, but existing schemes with predetermined worker populations do not directly adapt to worker arrivals and disconnections. To address these dynamics, we propose a dynamic CDC scheme that preserves surviving workers' caches and Reduce assignments while exploiting the storage brought by arriving clusters. The model accommodates general MapReduce tasks under a placement that is partly fixed and partly new. The scheme uses Cartesian products of cluster-wise placement delivery arrays (PDAs) for file placement. A delivery-aware greedy algorithm reassigns abandoned Reduce functions, and a Communication Array allows workers with no Reduce function to serve as coded transmitters. For arbitrary feasible disconnections, the scheme's exact communication load is derived. A converse bound under one-shot communication shows that, in the absence of disconnections, the scheme lies within a factor of 2 of the lower bound under these assumptions when new clusters arrive, and within a factor of 4 otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Chenglin Li, Minquan Cheng, Youlong Wu

item.title: Randomization Beyond Deterministic Adaptivity in Parallel Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.03335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parallel samplers, including masked diffusion models, generate several coordinates per round from conditional marginals, and their accuracy depends on which coordinates are revealed together. A schedule can be improved in two natural ways: adaptively, by choosing later batches from the values already generated, or by randomization, by drawing the schedule at random. We show that randomization is strictly more powerful. For every $r \geq 1$ we construct a full-support distribution on $9r$ binary coordinates such that every deterministic three-round sampler, even with value-dependent batches and arbitrary product kernels, has forward Kullback-Leibler divergence at least $\gamma r - \log 4$ with $\gamma \approx 0.0966$, whereas drawing one of four fixed schedules with two fair bits drives the divergence below $18 r \beta^r$ with $\beta \approx 0.966$. Both samplers query conditionals of the same target. The separation holds for every fixed number of rounds $T \geq 2$, a strict advantage survives perturbations of the target and errors in the conditional predictor, and exact rational arithmetic certifies the gap at nine coordinates, where trained neural predictors preserve it. The mechanism is a hidden mixture: each schedule preserves the dependence pattern of one component, while no deterministic first batch can serve them all.
item.dc:creator: Da Li, Bo Jin, Xiaopeng Wei

item.title: Arithmetic of qudit dimensions governs erasure correction on the Fano plane and stabilizer-state entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2610.18905v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Qudit codes often inherit the parameters of qubit codes, but not necessarily their correctable erasures. We show that a code encoding one qudit of dimension D into seven such qudits that corrects every erasure Steane's code corrects exists exactly when D is a power of 2; for the qutrit color code, exactly when D is odd. This needs no stabilizer assumption: these codes are, up to local unitaries, stabilizer codes of qubits, respectively prime-power qudits. The two patterns differ in one line, which completes the Fano plane only where 1+1=0. As ideal secret sharing schemes, these codes exist exactly where classical ones do: entanglement does not help, unlike for Euler's 36 officers. The same arithmetic makes the entropy cones of qubit and odd-dimensional stabilizer states incomparable from six parties on. At five, the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, answering an open question.
item.dc:creator: Xidan Song, Ruifeng Cao

item.title: Affine and cyclic affine equivalence of rotation-symmetric S-boxes
item.description: arXiv:2203.00778v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A rotation-symmetric S-box on $n$ bits is a vectorial Boolean function that commutes with the right cyclic shift and is therefore determined by a single Boolean function. The map $\chi$ used in Keccak is a well-known example. Ordinary affine equivalence allows arbitrary invertible affine transformations, which need not preserve rotation symmetry. We introduce \emph{cyclic affine equivalence}, in which the implementing transformations each have an invertible $k$-circulant linear part with $\gcd(k,n)=1$ and a translation vector fixed by the shift. For $n\ge3$, the two relations give the same classes of rotation-symmetric permutations exactly when $n$ is an odd prime for which $2$ is a primitive root. In every other dimension $n\ge3$, explicit constructions exhibit affine classes containing several cyclic affine classes. We derive exact class-size formulas, count cyclic affine classes for $3\le n\le9$, and classify a four-bit family of $\chi$-siblings under both relations. Finally, we characterize when a permutation is affinely equivalent to a rotation-symmetric one and apply the criterion to the Ascon S-box.
item.dc:creator: Tron Omland, Pantelimon Stanica

item.title: Enumerating Complexity Revisited
item.description: arXiv:2312.04187v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the relation between deterministic and randomized $\textit{enumerating}$ Kolmogorov complexity of sets $S\subseteq \mathbb{N}$. Let $D(S)$ be the length of a shortest input on which a fixed optimal deterministic machine enumerates $S$, and let $ R(S) $ be the probability that a fixed optimal randomized machine enumerates $S$. It is easy to see that $-\log R(S) \le D(S)+O(\log D(S))$ for every $S$; the converse direction is much harder. Solovay proved $D(S)\le -3\log R(S) +O(\log\log\frac{1}{ R(S) })$ for all $S$, while for finite sets the sharper bound with the constant $2$ is known. We show that the case of infinite sets carries no extra cost: $\textit{any}$ inequality of the form $D(F)\le -\alpha\log R(F)+O(\log\log\frac{1}{R(F)})$ with a computable $\alpha$, valid for all finite $F$, automatically extends to all sets. More generally, we prove a single dichotomy from which such transfer results follow for an arbitrary computable non-decreasing bound, and which also shows that every c.e. set $S$ has a finite subset $F$ such that $F$ has at least as large deterministic complexity as $S$ but randomized one approximately the same or lower. Our result makes qualitative progress on a problem studied by Solovay in 1977 by showing that the search for the optimal constant can be reduced to a purely combinatorial question about a game played with finite sets. In particular, our result yields $D(S)\le-2\log R(S) +O(\log\log\frac{1}{ R(S) })$ for every $S$, improving Solovay's constant $3$ to $2$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Shekhovtsov, Georgii Zakharov, Nikolay Vereshchagin

item.title: New classes of reversible cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2411.00721v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cellular automata find applications in cryptography, error correction, theoretical computer science, and the simulation of physical and biological processes. We say that a Boolean function is a proper lifting if its induced cellular automaton is reversible. This paper introduces new classes of proper liftings, constructed through compositions of landscape functions, and explores their cryptographic potential by computing indicators relevant to differential and linear cryptanalysis. We combine theoretical and computational methods to obtain a complete classification of proper liftings for diameters up to $6$. Several open problems and conjectures are posed along the way.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kristian Haugland, Tron Omland

item.title: Competing Bandits in Matching Markets via Super Stability
item.description: arXiv:2506.15926v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study bandit learning in matching markets with two-sided reward uncertainty, extending prior research primarily focused on single-sided uncertainty. Building on Irving's (1994) concept of super-stability and the partial-order proposal algorithm of Cseh and Juhos (2021), we use a simultaneous Extended Gale-Shapley procedure to certify stable matchings from incomplete preference information. By employing this procedure, our centralized algorithm attains logarithmic pessimal stable regret dependent on an instance-dependent admissible gap parameter. This algorithm is further adapted to a decentralized setting with a time-independent additive $O(N^3K)$ regret increase under the stated shared-flag communication model. Finally, we establish a centralized instance-dependent lower bound for binary stable regret on strict interior Bernoulli instances, elucidating the roles of admissible partial ranks and super-stable matching in characterizing the complexity of stable matching with bandit feedback.
item.dc:creator: Soumya Basu

item.title: A Survey on Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces: Fundamentals, Recent Advances, and Challenges
item.description: arXiv:2603.05633v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade several closely spaced programmable metasurface layers so that an electromagnetic wave undergoes repeated modulation-propagation interactions before leaving the stack. The stack thereby implements, at the speed of propagation and with few radio-frequency chains, high-dimensional analog transformations that would otherwise require digital precoding, combining, spatial filtering, focusing, or inference. Since 2023, SIM research has produced more than two hundred articles, a dedicated magazine special issue, and two survey-level overviews organized around applications and wave-domain computing. This article complements them with a model-to-hardware perspective. First, we present the electromagnetic modeling hierarchy of SIMs, making explicit the assumptions under which the models coincide, their validity regimes, and their computational complexity, with a common notation for hardware non-idealities and power consumption. Second, we present a methodology-first taxonomy (SIM-aware channel acquisition, model-based optimization, statistical-CSI design, learning-based control, and hardware-aware robust design), compare the families in terms of CSI requirements, complexity, convergence, and hardware constraints, and reconcile conflicting findings in the literature. Third, we synthesize applications by the physical role of the SIM. Fourth, we quantitatively compare experimentally demonstrated multilayer prototypes, separate validated from conceptual architectures, and discuss thermal, tolerance, and calibration issues. Fifth, we provide a tutorial-style performance and trade-off analysis anchored in reported results. Finally, we map evidence-based challenges to research directions with measurable targets. Lessons learned are summarized at the end of every section.

item.title: Empirical Ciphertext Distinguishability Testing of KEMs and Hybrid Encryption via Deep Learning
item.description: arXiv:2604.06942v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We model indistinguishability under chosen-plaintext attack (IND-CPA) games as binary classification tasks for deep neural networks (DNNs). We apply this methodology to the public-key encryption (PKE) schemes used to construct PQC key encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs) such as ML-KEM and HQC, and to cascaded symmetric algorithms, demonstrating methodological generality. Moreover, we present a novel extension of this approach to empirical distinguishability testing of hybrid KEMs. For IND-CPA-secure schemes and their combinations, no DNN achieves accuracy significantly different from random guessing (measured via Bonferroni-corrected binomial tests), consistent with theoretical security guarantees. For insecure schemes, such as plain RSA, AES-CTR and AES-CBC with IV or counter reuse, or RC4, the DNNs classify the ciphertexts better than random guessing. Thus, this framework is shown to serve as a practical, scheme-agnostic tool for flagging distinguishable ciphertexts in both individual and composed constructions.
item.dc:creator: Simon Calderon, Niklas Johansson, Onur G\"unl\"u

item.title: On the regularity index of the minimum distance function in projective nested Cartesian codes
item.description: arXiv:2604.20729v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a projective nested product of fields and let $\delta_X(d)$ be the minimum distance in degree $d\geq 1$ of the projective nested Cartesian code $C_X(d)$. The regularity index ${\rm reg}(\delta_X)$ of the minimum distance function $\delta_X$ is the minimum integer $d_0\geq 0$ such that $\delta_X(d)=1$ for $d\geq d_0$. We give a formula for ${\rm reg}(\delta_X)$ by determining an indicator function of least degree for each point of $X$ and using the fact that ${\rm reg}(\delta_X)$ is the ${\rm v}$-number of the vanishing ideal $I_X$ of $X$. Then we give an arithmetical criterion that characterizes when $X$ is Cayley--Bacharach.
item.dc:creator: Cicero Carvalho, Maria Vaz Pinto, Rafael H. Villarreal

item.title: Entropy Bounds for Local Coordination and Graph Amenability
item.description: arXiv:2606.01963v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study local coordination on finite graphs, equivalently, the ability of randomized local protocols with independent private randomness to produce highly correlated outputs at neighboring vertices. Hutchcroft, Rospuskova, and Tamuz (2026) showed that if such local coordination can be achieved with low cost, then the graph admits a low-cost leader profile, or equivalently an appropriate bounded-radius decomposition, with a square-root loss in the cost. We substantially improve this bound for unbiased binary outputs. If the average disagreement is $\varepsilon$, we construct a leader profile of cost $O(\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon))$. The key ingredient is an information-theoretic influence measure: after fixing an ordering of the independent information sources, we assign to each binary output the increments of mutual information revealed along that ordering. For two outputs that disagree with probability $p$, the corresponding measures are within binary entropy $h(p)$ in total variation. Combined with a grand coupling theorem, this yields the improved bound. We also show that a universal linear bound is impossible. We construct graphs with binary local profiles of cost $O(\varepsilon)$ for which every leader profile has cost $$ \Omega\!\left(\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}\right). $$ The construction uses weighted majority functions and can be implemented as an action-symmetric Nash equilibrium, giving a negative answer to the question of HRT whether leader equilibria are always optimal up to a constant factor. Finally, we show that the binary assumption is essential: for general real-valued outputs, the square-root dependence of the HRT theorem is sharp up to a universal constant.
item.dc:creator: Ron Peretz, Dean Kraizberg

item.title: Algebraic-Geometric Parvaresh--Vardy Subspace Designs and Rank Condensers
item.description: arXiv:2609.32834v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A subspace design is a collection of subspaces $H_1,\ldots,H_n$ of $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ with the property that no low-dimensional subspace $W$ intersects the collection "too much". Subspace designs and related objects in linear-algebraic pseudorandomness have found a broad range of applications, ranging from list decoding to derandomizing algorithms. We construct explicit strong subspace designs over every finite field. In the extremal case where the co-dimension $t$ of each $H_i$ is equal to the dimension of $W$, for every constant field size our construction attains $n=\Omega(k)$ and matches the probabilistic intersection bound up to a constant factor. All previous constructions required the field size to grow with $t$ (or $k$). Our subspace designs also imply new constructions of rank condensers over arbitrary finite fields. This result is the first to achieve an optimal dependence on $k$ while maintaining both a constant output entropy rate and a constant field size. As an application, we construct lossless rank extractors for linear sources of rank $r$, for all $r < q$, with parameters matching those of Guo, Raj, Shangguan and Zhang (FOCS '26), thereby generalizing their result to prime fields and smaller field sizes. Our construction is based on an algebraic-geometric version of the Parvaresh--Vardy codes (Parvaresh--Vardy FOCS '05, Guruswami ECCC '05), extending the framework underlying the condensers of Guruswami, Umans and Vadhan (JACM '09). We view our construction as a linear-algebraic analysis -- tailored to affine sources -- of the GUV construction, generalized to functions over algebraic curves. More specifically, inspired by Ta-Shma and Umans (CCC '12) we develop a two-level evaluation scheme, where we first evaluate a function on a curve at extension-field points, and then evaluate a corresponding affine-linear polynomial to obtain outputs over the base field.
item.dc:creator: Gil Cohen, Dean Doron, Noam Goldgraber

item.title: Short-Length Code Designs for Integrated Sensing and Communications: A Deep Learning Approach
item.description: arXiv:2609.33605v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables joint communication and sensing using a shared waveform, but its signal design is challenging due to the inherent trade-off between the two objectives, particularly in the short blocklength regime. This paper proposes an autoencoder (AE)-based framework for ISAC waveform design in noncoherent settings. We derive a modified Cram\'er-Rao bound for multi-target delay estimation and analyze the maximum-likelihood decoding rule for noncoherent communication under correlated fading. These results reveal structural connections and trade-offs between communication and sensing objectives in waveform design. Based on this analysis, the AE learns waveform representations that jointly optimize both functionalities, with a tunable parameter controlling the trade-off. Simulation results show that the proposed design outperforms conventional schemes in both communication reliability and sensing accuracy, especially under short blocklength and fading conditions.
item.dc:creator: Muah Kim, Shuangyang Li, Tayyebeh Jahani-Nezhad, Rafael F. Schaefer, Giuseppe Caire

item.title: Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube
item.description: arXiv:2610.12358v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a known finite-dimensional model subspace, classical Gaussian regression theory guarantees that least squares eventually attains the parametric rate, with prediction error scaling as the subspace dimension divided by the sample size. Yet subspaces with the same number of unknown coefficients can require very different sample sizes to reach this regime. For subspaces of polynomials on the Boolean cube, a fundamental question is how restrictions on degree and ambient dimension jointly determine this threshold. Our main result sharply characterizes the worst-subspace minimax sample threshold over a substantial parameter range, revealing an exponential dependence on degree and precisely quantifying the joint effects of degree, ambient dimension, and subspace dimension. A small modification of our lower-bound construction reveals a strong separation: a single subspace can admit noiseless recovery with optimal sample complexity independent of degree, yet require essentially the worst-case sample size, exponential in degree, to attain the noisy parametric rate. To establish the sampling lower bound, we sharpen the Polyanskiy-Samorodnitsky uncertainty principle (J. Funct. Anal., '19) to uniformly optimal precision and extend its concentration guarantee to large subspaces in which every function concentrates most of its energy on one shared Hamming ball. The sampling upper bound follows from the sharp moment bound of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, '21) combined with empirical-process bounds.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Weinberger

item.title: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting
item.description: arXiv:2610.20079v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In undirected multiple-unicast networks, where independent messages are sent between specified source--destination pairs, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, whereas fractional routing splits and forwards individual messages along paths without mixing them. Proposed in 2004 by Li and Li and independently by Harvey, Kleinberg, and Lehman, the multiple-unicast conjecture---a central conjecture in network coding with deep connections to computational complexity---asserts that network coding and fractional routing have the same achievable rate region. We construct a counterexample refuting this conjecture and use it to reduce block transfers in external-memory data rearrangement, thereby accelerating external-memory integer sorting and answering in the affirmative the longstanding question of Aggarwal and Vitter (1988) on whether integer operations can beat the comparison-sorting input/output (I/O) bound. Specifically, we give a deterministic sorting algorithm: for $N$ integers of $\Theta(\log N)$ bits, a memory holding $M$ integers, and block transfers of $B$ integers, where $2B\le M\le N$, the number of block transfers is \[ O\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+ \frac{\log N}{(\log(M/B))^{1-\varepsilon}(\log M)^\varepsilon} \right]\right), \] where $\varepsilon=1.5\times10^{-5}$ is an absolute constant. This bound asymptotically improves on the classical $\Theta\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+ \frac{\log(N/M)}{\log(M/B)}\right]\right)$ comparison-sorting bound in certain parameter regimes. Under the external-memory model specified in this paper, we have formally verified the algorithm's correctness and I/O complexity bound in Lean~4.
item.dc:creator: Baochun Li, Zongpeng Li, Sirui Liu

item.title: Keep Pace to Learn: Movable-Antenna Compensation of Channel Aging in Over-the-Air Split Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.23118v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Split learning (SL) trains a neural network across devices by exchanging intermediate activations and gradients. In over-the-air SL, the wireless channel serves as an inter-layer linear map, and when the forward and backward channels match, reciprocity and conjugation supply the backward product without channel estimation at the base station (BS). Passive user motion, which the learning link does not control, breaks this match. Movable antennas let the antenna move relative to the user device, and we use this freedom to compensate the displacement. For a stationary BS and a propagation environment quasi-static within each exchange, returning the antenna to its forward-transmission position restores the channel and yields a conditionally unbiased gradient estimate. We also derive when discrete positioning or mechanical movement can achieve this in time. A residual displacement below a quarter wavelength keeps the real part of the channel correlation positive for any angular spectrum. At zero effective offset, independent Gaussian jitter attenuates this correlation without reversing its sign, whereas a persistent offset can reverse it, and in arrays the tolerance depends on the receive-combining direction. These effects enter a nonconvex convergence bound, and a local analysis shows that partial mechanical compensation saves cycle time to first order at only a second-order loss in correlation. In CIFAR-10 experiments, a user terminal without channel state information stays at chance level under uncompensated walking motion, while discrete positioning stays within about 0.3 percentage points of exact restoration, including at a speed beyond the modeled actuator's limit.
item.dc:creator: Xianzhong Li, Yuzhi Yang, Tianhao Guo, Zhaoyang Zhang

item.title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodictive tests: a unifying classical variational principle
item.description: arXiv:2610.29696v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A single classical f-divergence has several inequivalent quantum versions, but what distinguishes them operationally is less clear. Matsumoto's reverse tests characterize the maximal quantum f-divergence as the least classical distinguishability needed to prepare two quantum states with one device. Here we introduce retrodictive tests, in which two reverse tests sharing a reference state are coupled via Bayesian retrodiction to define a forward and a reverse stochastic process. In the forward process, the system is prepared by the first device and measured by the Petz transpose of the second; the reverse process interchanges their roles. We seek the least classical distinguishability between these two processes, as measured by the f-divergence between their joint laws, for fixed prescribed states and reference. For full-rank states in finite dimension, we prove that the canonical spectral implementations attain this minimum simultaneously for every operator-convex f. The reference then determines which quantum f-divergence is obtained: a flat reference gives the standard divergences, with the Nussbaum--Szko{\l}a distributions as optimal joint laws; either prescribed state as reference recovers Matsumoto's reverse tests and the maximal divergences; and power references give the geodesic family. In particular, the Umegaki and Belavkin--Staszewski relative entropies arise from the same classical variational principle under different choices of reference. Spectral optimality extends to processes containing a quantum channel; for channels with full-rank Choi operator, the minimum of the forward relative entropy agrees with a known average entropy production.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Buscemi

item.title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic
item.description: arXiv:2610.39110v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame, resolve the aliasing in only one dimension, and assume integer delays and Doppler shifts. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel with fractional delays and Doppler shifts, using the same bandwidth and frame size. We show that modular arithmetic on the peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers maintain a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel estimation error among all the compared systems. In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC outperforms all baselines, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Novero, Mudasir Ahmad Sheikh, Danish Nisar, Saif Khan Mohammed, Michele Zorzi, Robert Calderbank
